Study_Title: AEGIS: No Tool Call Left Unchecked -- A Pre-Execution Firewall and Audit Layer for AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection, malicious shell/SQL/file/network tool arguments, SSRF, path traversal, and credential exfiltration across 14 LLM agent frameworks lacking pre-execution mediation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Ed25519 digital signatures and SHA-256 hash chaining (H(trace_n) = SHA256(data_n || H(trace_{n-1}))) over a three-stage pre-execution firewall (deep string extraction, 22-pattern risk scanner across 7 categories, and composable policy validation with human-in-the-loop hold).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Aegis Pre-Execution Firewall & Audit Layer interposing synchronously between agent runtime tool dispatch and external tool execution (Figure 1, p. 2).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Deterministic pre-execution blocking/escalation of policy-violating tool calls and tamper-evident post-hoc forensic auditability via Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 hash chains.
Trust_Assumptions: Host environment, Aegis interceptor hook, Ed25519 signing keys, and human approval operator remain uncompromised; agent reasoning cannot bypass the wrapped tool-execution path.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Blocks 100% of attacks (48/48 curated attack instances across 7 categories), yields 1.2% false positive rate on 500 benign tool calls (6/500), and adds 8.3 ms median interception latency across 1,000 consecutive tool calls across 14 frameworks in Python, JS, and Go (Abstract p. 1, Table 1 p. 3, Section 4 pp. 3–4).
Exposed_Security_Function: Pre-execution tool-call firewall (allow/block/hold-for-human) and Ed25519 + SHA-256 hash-chained compliance audit trail export (PDF/CSV).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Pattern-based 22-rule risk scanner may miss novel semantic obfuscation or unseen attack variants (explicitly noted p. 4); relies on pre-quantum Ed25519 signatures for audit trail non-repudiation.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 2–4 (pp. 2–4): "High-risk calls can be held for human approval, and all decisions are recorded in a tamper-evident audit trail based on Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 hash chaining... On a curated suite of 48 attack instances, Aegis blocks all attacks in the suite before execution; on 500 benign tool calls, it yields a 1.2% false positive rate; and across 1,000 consecutive interceptions, it adds 8.3 ms median latency."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Aegis interposes a 3-stage pre-execution firewall and Ed25519/SHA-256 hash-chained audit layer across 14 agent frameworks, blocking 48/48 attacks with 1.2% FPR on 500 benign calls and 8.3 ms median latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical evaluation on a 48-attack / 500-benign curated suite and 1,000-call latency benchmark across 14 frameworks (12 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent tool-call arguments (shell, SQL, filesystem, network) and execution audit logs.
Composition_Evidence: Connects human escalation gates (B1), pre-execution tool firewalling (B3), and Ed25519 + SHA-256 tamper-evident audit logging (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (12 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur Aegis (3-stage firewall + Ed25519/SHA-256 hash chain) beserta metrik RQ3 (48/48 blokir, 1.2% FPR, 8.3 ms median latency) dan dependensi RQ4 (Ed25519 STAGE_0).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 12 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Formalizing the Safety, Security, and Functional Properties of Agentic AI Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-protocol architectural misalignment between vertical tool access (MCP) and horizontal agent delegation (A2A), resulting in task handoff failures, inconsistent state management, circular delegation deadlocks, prompt injection, and proxy privilege escalation (Section 3, pp. 3–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Computation Tree Logic / CTL formal state-machine specification of Host Agent Model H = (A, E, T, R, C, O, CL, S_H) and 11-state Task Lifecycle Model L = (S_t, s_0, E_t, delta) enforcing 30 temporal logic properties HP1–HP16 and TL1–TL14).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Host Agent Core (HAC), Registry (R), Orchestrator DAG (O), and Communication Layer (CL) across A2A and MCP boundaries (Figures 1–2, pp. 5, 7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 30 CTL formal properties (16 Host Agent properties HP1–HP16 in Table 1, p. 6; 14 Task Lifecycle properties TL1–TL14 in Table 2, p. 8) guaranteeing liveness, safety (HP7–HP11, TL6–TL10), completeness, fairness, and reachability.
Trust_Assumptions: Host Agent Orchestrator, Registry discovery validation V_M(EE), and deterministic state transition function delta : S_t x E_t -> S_t accurately govern runtime sub-task execution.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: No empirical runtime latency or model-checking execution overhead reported; provides 30 CTL specifications (HP1–HP16 in Table 1 p. 6; TL1–TL14 in Table 2 p. 8) and qualitative case analyses (Section 6, pp. 9–10).
Exposed_Security_Function: Unified CTL formal specification of Host Agent orchestration (HP1–HP16) and 11-state sub-task lifecycle transitions (TL1–TL14) across MCP and A2A.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Purely formal CTL specification without automated model-checker synthesis benchmarks, cryptographic binding, or empirical runtime overhead evaluation on live LLM agent deployments (Section 7, p. 10).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1), Section 4.1–4.2 (pp. 4–7), & Tables 1–2 (pp. 6, 8): "Grounded in this framework, we define 16 properties for the host agent and 14 for the task lifecycle, categorized into liveness, safety, completeness, and fairness. Expressed in temporal logic, these properties enable formal verification of system behavior, detection of coordination edge cases, and prevention of deadlocks and security vulnerabilities."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Introduces a unified Host Agent Model H and 11-state Task Lifecycle Model L across MCP and A2A protocols, specifying 30 CTL properties (HP1–HP16 and TL1–TL14) for liveness, safety, completeness, fairness, and reachability.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal CTL modeling framework and 30 property specifications published at ICLR 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild (13 pp.).
Protected_Object: Host Agent Task DAG D, Registry capability profiles R(E), and sub-task lifecycle state transitions across MCP and A2A.
Composition_Evidence: Explicitly models composition of user intent resolution (B1: HAC Req_U -> I_U), horizontal A2A agent delegation (B2), and vertical MCP tool invocation (B3) via DAG precedence invariants HP7–HP11 and TL6–TL10.
Coding_Rationale: Audit ulang baris pilot CLM-0031 dari PDF teks lengkap (13 hlm.) dan resolusi status UNMAPPED pada register menjadi MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3). Memperbaiki locator seksi (Section 4–5, Tables 1–2 hlm. 4–8) dan Formal_Evidence_Type menjadi FORMAL_MODEL (spesifikasi CTL HP1–HP16 & TL1–TL14 tanpa bukti teorema mekanis).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0031 telah diaudit ulang dari PDF teks lengkap 13 hlm. dan status UNMAPPED telah dipetakan ke B1;B2;B3).

Study_Title: Authenticated Workflows: A Systems Approach to Protecting Agentic AI
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, confused-deputy privilege escalation, unauthorized tool invocation, data exfiltration, and multi-hop workflow tampering across 9 enterprise agent frameworks (MCP, A2A, OpenAI, Claude, LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, LlamaIndex, Haystack).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ECDSA-256 (P-256) digital signatures over workflow attestations, SHA-256 hash chains for audit logs, Merkle trees for policy store integrity, and MAPL (Monotonic Agent Policy Language) enforcing monotonic permission intersection pi(P_1 cap P_2) = pi(P_1) cap pi(P_2).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Distributed Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) embedded at four fundamental boundaries: prompts, tools, data, and context across 9 agent frameworks via thin adapters (Section 3, pp. 3–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 (Monotonic Restriction, p. 4), Theorem 2 (Workflow Integrity), and Lemma 6 (Completeness & Minimality of 4 control surfaces, p. 2): deterministic cryptographic rejection of unauthenticated or policy-violating operations across workflow hops.
Trust_Assumptions: Minimal Trusted Computing Base (Policy Administration Point, Merkle policy store, ECDSA-256 key store, and PEPs) is uncompromised; cryptographic primitives (ECDSA-256, SHA-256) are unforgeable/collision-resistant.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: 100% recall with 0% false positives across 174 test cases, mitigation of 9/10 OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 risks (Table 2, p. 12) and 2 production CVEs, O(log M + N) policy scaling vs O(M*N), and <0.2 ms cryptographic overhead per operation (ECDSA-256 sign ~102 us, verification ~89 us, SHA-256 hash chain update <15 us on 8-core 16GB RAM, p. 13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Authenticated Workflows runtime PEP, MAPL hierarchical monotonic policy engine, ECDSA-256 workflow dependency attestation, and SHA-256/Merkle audit log.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical ECDSA-256 (P-256) signatures vulnerable to Shor's algorithm (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY); leaves OWASP LLM06/model supply-chain poisoning outside runtime boundary scope (Table 2, p. 12).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 6 (p. 13): "Empirical validation shows 100% recall with zero false positives across 174 test cases, protection against 9 of 10 OWASP Top 10 risks, and complete mitigation of two high impact production CVEs... <0.2ms overhead (ECDSA signature generation ~102 us, verification ~89 us, hash chain updates <15 us per operation)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Authenticated Workflows and MAPL enforce monotonic policy intersection and ECDSA-256/SHA-256/Merkle cryptographic attestations across 4 boundaries in 9 frameworks with <0.2 ms overhead and 100% recall / 0% FPR on 174 test cases.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal proofs (Theorems 1–2, Lemma 6) and empirical evaluation across 174 test cases and 9 frameworks (18 pp.).
Protected_Object: Prompts, tool invocations, data access paths, and multi-agent workflow context attestations.
Composition_Evidence: Proves Theorem 1 (Monotonic Restriction: effective policy across chained nodes Node 1 -> Node 2 is intersection P_1 cap P_2, p. 4 & p. 17) with ECDSA-256 workflow dependency attestations.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (18 hlm.). Mencakup bukti formal (Theorem 1 Monotonic Restriction, Lemma 6), metrik mikrobenchmark RQ3 (<0.2 ms overhead: sign 102 us, verify 89 us, hash <15 us; 100% recall / 0% FPR pada 174 kasus), dan dependensi RQ4 (ECDSA-256 STAGE_0).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 18 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Zero-Knowledge Audit for Internet of Agents: Privacy-Preserving Communication Verification with Model Context Protocol
Threat_Attacker_Model: Honest-but-curious or untrusted agents and third-party Audit Service Providers (ASPs) attempting to eavesdrop on private MCP message payloads or forge communication billing/compliance records in Internet of Agents (IoA) ecosystems.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Groth16 / Circom zk-SNARK zero-knowledge proofs over Poseidon cryptographic commitments and MCP JSON-RPC message structure constraints (MAX_JSON=64 bytes, MAX_TYPE=20 bytes, NUM_TYPES=8, Table III, p. 10).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Asynchronous zk-MCP Prover and Audit Service Provider (ASP) verification layer integrated alongside bidirectional Model Context Protocol (MCP) channels (Figures 1–2, pp. 3–5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 (Completeness & Soundness, p. 7) and Theorem 2 (Zero-Knowledge Communication Privacy, p. 7): mutual verifiable auditing of MCP message schema/type compliance and usage metrics without revealing plaintext message contents.
Trust_Assumptions: Trusted setup for Circom/Groth16 zk-SNARK circuits is uncompromised; Poseidon hash is collision-resistant; asynchronous commitment anchoring binds live MCP messages.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Asynchronous out-of-band proof generation adds 0 ms inline MCP communication latency; zk-SNARK verification time remains <4.5 ms per proof (circuit size MAX_JSON=64B, MAX_TYPE=20B, NUM_TYPES=8, Section V, pp. 9–11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Privacy-preserving mutual MCP communication audit (zk-MCP) via Circom zk-SNARK proof generation and asynchronous ASP verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on compact circuit payload bounds (MAX_JSON=64 bytes, Table III p. 10); relies on pairing-based zk-SNARKs (Groth16) requiring a trusted setup and vulnerable to quantum adversaries (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section V (pp. 9–10): "We fully implement the framework, including Circom-based zero-knowledge proof generation and an audit protocol integrated with MCP's bidirectional channel... Message storage and parsing occur asynchronously in parallel with MCP communication, ensuring that MCP communication latency is not affected."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: zk-MCP integrates Circom zk-SNARKs with MCP to provide privacy-preserving mutual communication auditing with <4.5 ms verification overhead and zero inline MCP communication latency impact.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal security proofs (Theorems 1–2) and Circom zk-SNARK prototype evaluation for MCP message auditing (13 pp.).
Protected_Object: MCP bidirectional JSON-RPC communication payloads, message type metadata, and billing/compliance audit trails.
Composition_Evidence: Decouples synchronous MCP message exchange from asynchronous zk-SNARK audit proof generation and verification at the B4 audit boundary.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (13 hlm.). Memvalidasi protokol zk-MCP berbasis Circom zk-SNARK (Theorems 1–2 hlm. 7, Table III–IV hlm. 7 & 10), overhead verifikasi <4.5 ms, dan klasifikasi PQC STAGE_0 untuk zk-SNARK berbasis kurva eliptik.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 13 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: AgentWard: A Lifecycle Security Architecture for Autonomous AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-stage lifecycle attack chains on autonomous AI agents (OpenClaw), including trojanized/obfuscated third-party skills at initialization, indirect prompt injection at input ingestion, persistent memory poisoning (MEMORY.md/AGENTS.md), objective drift at decision, and privileged shell/file exfiltration at execution (Section II, pp. 2–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Five-layer defense-in-depth runtime architecture: Foundation Scan, Input Sanitization, Cognition Protection, Decision Alignment, and Execution Control with eBPF system monitoring and session-level shared risk state).
Enforcement_Point_Location: OpenClaw bidirectional plugin hooks: before_prompt_build (Foundation Scan), before_message_write (Input Sanitization & Decision Alignment), and before_tool_call (Cognition Protection on memory files & Execution Control on all tools, Section IV-A, p. 5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cross-lifecycle threat containment and risk-accumulating fail-safe execution governance across Initialization, Input, Memory, Decision, and Execution boundaries (Table I, p. 4).
Trust_Assumptions: OpenClaw host runtime, bidirectional plugin adapter hooks, session-level security state store, and eBPF kernel monitor cannot be bypassed or modified by untrusted skills.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: No quantitative latency or throughput table reported; qualitatively validated via an open-source OpenClaw plugin prototype (https://github.com/FIND-Lab/AgentWard) across 2 multi-stage attack case studies (Malicious Skill to Data Exfiltration; Indirect Prompt Injection to Persistent MEMORY.md Backdoor & DoS, Section IV-B, pp. 5–7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Five-layer lifecycle security hooks (Foundation Scan, Input Sanitization, Cognition Protection, Decision Alignment, Execution Control) with cross-layer session risk accumulation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly omits quantitative benchmark totals, false-positive rates, and runtime latency measurements (p. 5: "emphasis is on control placement... rather than on benchmark totals"); relies on LLM-judge response review at the Decision Alignment layer.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Section III-B Table I (p. 4) & Section IV-A (p. 5): "Concretely, Foundation Scan is attached to before_prompt_build. Input Sanitization and Decision Alignment are attached to before_message_write... Cognition Protection and Execution Control are attached to before_tool_call... The emphasis is on control placement, cross-layer coordination, and operational implication rather than on benchmark totals."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AgentWard organizes autonomous agent security into five coordinated lifecycle layers (Foundation Scan, Input Sanitization, Cognition Protection, Decision Alignment, Execution Control) implemented as a plugin-native prototype on OpenClaw.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Architectural blueprint, 5-layer OpenClaw plugin prototype, and 2 multi-stage attack chain case studies without quantitative benchmark tables (11 pp.).
Protected_Object: Skill manifests/dependencies, active working context, persistent memory files (MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md), action plans, and host environment tools.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates cross-stage risk propagation and shared security context escalation from Foundation Scan/Input Sanitization (B1/B2) through Cognition Protection (B4 memory) and Decision Alignment to Execution Control (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Audit ulang baris pilot CLM-0032 dari PDF teks lengkap (11 hlm.) dan resolusi status UNMAPPED pada register menjadi MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4). Memperbarui Implementation_Maturity menjadi OPEN_SOURCE_COMMIT (tersedia repo GitHub FIND-Lab/AgentWard pada catatan kaki 1 hlm. 5) dan mencatat ketiadaan tabel kuantitatif (DG;AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0032 telah diaudit ulang dari PDF teks lengkap 11 hlm. dan status UNMAPPED telah dipetakan ke B1;B2;B3;B4).

Study_Title: MAGIQ: A Post-Quantum Multi-Agentic AI Governance System with Provable Security
Threat_Attacker_Model: Quantum-capable (PPT + QPT) adversaries attempting to forge agent identities, bypass owner communication/access-control policy budgets, violate one-to-one or one-to-many session governance, or repudiate inter-agent messages (Section 3, pp. 4–5).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Post-quantum NIST-standardized primitives: ML-KEM (CRYSTALS-Kyber) for key encapsulation, ML-DSA (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) for digital signatures and policy/stamp attestations, and symmetric AEAD/PRF session channels within a Universal Composability (UC) framework.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Provider, Governance Entity (GE), and Agent local enforcement wrappers governing Registration (F_Reg), Agent Authentication (F_A-auth), Agent-to-Agent Sessions (F_Ases), and One-to-Many Sessions (F_Cses) (Sections 3–4, pp. 5–10).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 5.1 (UC Security in the (F_scs, F_CA, G_clk, G_h)-hybrid model, p. 10): provable post-quantum registration integrity, mutual authentication, session policy-budget enforcement, and non-repudiable message attribution.
Trust_Assumptions: Certificate Authority (F_CA), global clock (G_clk), and Random Oracle (G_h) hold; ML-KEM IND-CCA2 and ML-DSA EUF-CMA hardness assumptions hold against quantum adversaries; network DoS is out of scope (p. 4).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Measured post-quantum cryptographic overhead per A-session is t_crypto = 20.33 ms (Table 1, p. 12), achieving comparable or lower end-to-end multi-agent task execution time (in seconds) than the pre-quantum SAGA baseline due to amortized session-level policy stamps (Tables 1–3, pp. 11–13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Post-quantum agent registration, policy-budget stamp issuance, 1-to-1 and 1-to-many session key establishment, and accountable message attribution (MAGIQ).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Assumes an honest Certificate Authority (F_CA) and synchronized global clock (G_clk); network-layer denial-of-service (DoS) and internal LLM prompt-injection reasoning manipulation within an authorized budget are out of scope (Section 3, p. 4).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1), Theorem 5.1 (p. 10), & Section 6.2 Table 1 (p. 12): "Theorem 5.1. MAGIQ (Section 4) UC-realizes F_Reg, F_A-auth, F_Ases, and F_Cses in the (F_scs, F_CA, G_clk, G_h)-hybrid model... t_crypto = 20.33ms is the measured cryptographic overhead per A-session."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MAGIQ provides the first UC-secure post-quantum multi-agent AI governance framework for registration, authentication, 1-to-1/1-to-many session policy budgets, and message attribution with 20.33 ms crypto overhead per session.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Full UC formal security proofs (Theorem 5.1 & Lemmas) and empirical comparison against SAGA baseline (27 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent registration credentials, owner communication/access policy budgets, 1-to-1 and 1-to-many session keys, and inter-agent message attribution logs.
Composition_Evidence: Proves universal composability (Theorem 5.1, p. 10) across F_Reg, F_A-auth, F_Ases, and F_Cses in the (F_scs, F_CA, G_clk, G_h)-hybrid model.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (27 hlm.). Studi inti RQ4 (STAGE_2_PURE_PQC_PROPOSED) yang menggantikan protokol pra-kuantum SAGA dengan primitif pasca-kuantum dan membuktikan keamanan Universal Composability (Theorem 5.1 hlm. 10) serta membandingkan overhead (t_crypto = 20.33 ms, Table 1–3 hlm. 11–13).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 27 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: MAGIQ: A Post-Quantum Multi-Agentic AI Governance System with Provable Security

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Amortized post-quantum session policy tickets/stamps over ML-KEM and ML-DSA vs. SAGA's per-contact classical public-key handshake and ProVerif-verified messaging.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent-to-Agent (A-session) and One-to-Many (C-session) cryptographic handshake and policy-budget verification layer (Section 6, pp. 11–14).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantum-resistant session establishment and policy budget enforcement with bounded per-session cryptographic latency (20.33 ms) and scalable multi-agent task completion time.
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark testbed network and LLM agent task workloads accurately reflect multi-agent collaboration patterns.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Per-A-session post-quantum cryptographic overhead is 20.33 ms (Table 1, p. 12); total task execution time across multi-agent benchmarks (Tables 2–3, pp. 12–13) matches or improves upon SAGA by amortizing governance checks across session budgets.
Exposed_Security_Function: Comparative benchmark of post-quantum MAGIQ vs. classical SAGA across cryptographic operations, bandwidth, and end-to-end multi-agent task latency.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated in controlled multi-agent task benchmarks; larger post-quantum public-key and signature byte sizes increase initial registration/ticket bandwidth compared to ECC baselines.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Section 6.2 (pp. 11–13, Tables 1–3): "Table 1 reports the computational overhead of protocol operations in MAGIQ against the SAGA baseline... t_crypto = 20.33ms is the measured cryptographic overhead per A-session. Table 2 presents a direct comparison between SAGA and MAGIQ."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical evaluation of MAGIQ against SAGA demonstrates that post-quantum session governance incurs 20.33 ms cryptographic overhead per A-session while maintaining competitive end-to-end multi-agent task execution times.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled comparative benchmark of post-quantum MAGIQ vs. SAGA across computation, communication, and task latency (Section 6, pp. 11–14).
Protected_Object: Multi-agent session establishment latency and communication bandwidth under post-quantum migration.

Study_Title: Binding Agent ID: Unleashing the Power of AI Agents with accountability and credibility
Threat_Attacker_Model: Key compromise and arbitrary code/configuration substitution in traditional key-based agent authentication, where an attacker holding sk executes modified agent binaries or unauthorized operations without operator binding (Section 4.1, p. 13).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machine (zkVM, RISC Zero / SP1 STARK-to-SNARK recursive proofs) binding program binary imageID + local config Merkle proof (eth_getProof) + biometric operator authentication + zkTLS (AES-GCM) to an on-chain Ethereum smart contract (AgentID).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Local biometric binding module, Ethereum Agent Identity Smart Contract (registerUser, registerAgent), and zkVM Code-Level Authentication prover/verifier (Sections 3–5, pp. 5–16).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Properties 1–4 (pp. 14–15): Code-Identity Binding, Unforgeability of Execution Order (recursive zkVM state transitions), Configuration Integrity via Ethereum storage Merkle proofs, and Compact Verification.
Trust_Assumptions: zkVM soundness (collision-resistant hash and recursive proof system), Ethereum blockchain state finality, and local biometric hardware sensor integrity hold; external LLM API data authenticity requires zkTLS extension (p. 8, p. 15).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Hardhat EVM gas benchmark (Table 3, p. 10): registerUser = 390,325 gas, registerAgent = 507,763 gas, deregisterAgent = 124,117 gas, updateAgent = 128,837 gas; recursive zkVM proof generation and verification benchmarked across multi-step agent executions (Section 5, pp. 10–13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Binding Agent ID (BAID) on-chain lifecycle registry, biometric user-to-agent binding, and zkVM recursive code-execution provenance attestation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: zkVM cannot natively verify the semantic truth of external web/LLM API outputs without zkTLS (p. 8); Ethereum ECDSA transaction signatures and SNARK wrapper remain pre-quantum (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY); recursive zkVM proving incurs multi-second off-chain latency.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Table 3 (p. 10): "BAID integrates three orthogonal mechanisms: local binding via biometric authentication, decentralized on-chain identity management, and a novel zkVM-based Code-Level Authentication protocol... User Registration (registerUser) 390,325 gas; Agent Registration (registerAgent) 507,763 gas; Agent Deregistration (deregisterAgent) 124,117 gas; Agent Update (updateAgent) 128,837 gas."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: BAID binds physical operator biometrics, on-chain Ethereum AgentID smart contracts, and recursive zkVM code-level execution proofs to prevent agent code substitution and ensure execution accountability.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Prototype implementation on Hardhat/Ethereum and zkVM with gas consumption benchmarks and security property analysis (18 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent binary imageID, local configuration state (Config_local), operator identity binding, and multi-step execution provenance.
Composition_Evidence: Chains biometric operator intent binding (B1) to on-chain Merkle state proofs (eth_getProof) and recursive zkVM execution trace proofs (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (18 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur BAID (biometrik + smart contract Ethereum + zkVM recursive proofs + zkTLS extension) beserta tabel konsumsi gas (Table 3 hlm. 10) dan properti keamanan 1–4 (hlm. 14–15).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 18 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: ADR: An Agentic Detection System for Enterprise Agentic AI Security
Threat_Attacker_Model: Enterprise MCP agent attacks including indirect prompt injection, tool poisoning, credential exposure across 26 secret categories, and unauthorized command/file execution invisible to traditional host EDR tools.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Three-component Agentic AI Detection and Response system: ADR Sensor for causal MCP telemetry, ADR Explorer for automated red-teaming/hard-example synthesis, and two-tier ADR Detector combining fast triage with LLM context-aware reasoning).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Enterprise MCP client/server telemetry hooks (ADR Sensor) and two-tier online detection & shift-left secret prevention pipeline deployed across Uber developer/enterprise hosts (Section 2–4, pp. 2–8).

Study_Title: Proof of Execution: Runtime Verification for Governed AI Agent Actions

Enforcement_Point_Location: Prime Execution Model (PEM) Gateway, Effector (exclusive holder of external mutation credentials), Recorder (Merkle-sealed ECES), and Validator (Sections 3–5, pp. 3–8).

Exposed_Security_Function: Proof of Execution (PoE) validator checking 5 invariants (I1–I5a), Merkle-sealed Execution Causal Event Stream (ECES), and Execution Attestation Certificate (EAC) issuance.

Study_Title: Structural Representations for Cross-Attack Generalization in AI Agent Threat Detection
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-attack generalization failure in AI agent threat detection where attackers deploy unseen structural attacks (tool hijacking, data exfiltration, privilege escalation) alongside linguistic attacks (social engineering, prompt injection) across multi-step tool traces.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Deterministic rule-based Structural Tokenization Algorithm 1 encoding execution-flow patterns—tool calls, argument types, observation structures—combined with Gated Multi-View Fusion over structural and conversational views).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Behavioral trace anomaly detector operating over multi-step agent tool-invocation trajectories (Section 3, pp. 2–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cross-attack out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization across structural and linguistic agent attack families without sacrificing in-distribution (IID) detection accuracy.
Trust_Assumptions: Agent execution harness logs true tool-call names, arguments, and observation structures into behavioral traces visible to the detector.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Standard conversational tokenization fails on structural attacks (AUC 0.39 on tool hijacking, AUC 0.46 on data exfiltration vs 0.78 on social engineering); Structural Tokenization improves OOD AUC by +46 points on tool hijacking (to 0.85), +39 points on data exfiltration (to 0.85), +71 points on unknown attacks, and +6 points IID; Gated Multi-View Fusion achieves AUC 0.89 on social engineering while preserving structural detection (Abstract p. 1, Section 4 pp. 4–6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Structural trace tokenizer (Algorithm 1) and Gated Multi-View Fusion classifier for multi-step agent behavioral trace threat detection.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 6 (p. 7) notes that the deterministic rule-based structural tokenizer (Algorithm 1) can be targeted by adaptive adversaries who mimic benign tool-call sequence structures while embedding malicious payloads inside allowed parameters.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "We discover that standard conversational tokenization—capturing linguistic patterns from agent interactions—fails catastrophically on structural attacks like tool hijacking (AUC 0.39) and data exfiltration (AUC 0.46)... This simple representational change dramatically improves cross-attack generalization: +46 AUC points on tool hijacking, +39 points on data exfiltration, and +71 points on unknown attacks, while simultaneously improving in-distribution performance (+6 points)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Structural Tokenization and Gated Multi-View Fusion encode agent execution-flow patterns rather than surface text, improving cross-attack OOD detection AUC by +46 points on tool hijacking, +39 points on data exfiltration, and +71 points on unknown attacks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled IID and OOD cross-attack generalization experiments across structural and linguistic agent attack families (8 pp.).
Protected_Object: Multi-step agent behavioral execution traces (tool calls, arguments, observations).
Composition_Evidence: Monitors multi-step tool-invocation execution flows (B3) and behavioral audit traces (B4) to detect cross-turn structural attacks.

Study_Title: OCELOT: Inference-Leakage Budgets for Privacy-Preserving LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cumulative inference-based PII/secret leakage across multi-step trajectories to honest-but-curious or colluding external tool/service sinks, compounded by bidirectional indirect prompt injection turning the agent or local defender LLM against the user (Section 2, pp. 2–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Per-trajectory Merkle-chained leakage ledger L signed with verifier key sk_V, combined with Witness-Verified Declassification (WVD) over 5 declassification operators (Table 1, p. 7) and credal posterior min-entropy audit.
Enforcement_Point_Location: OCELOT Runtime Mediator & Deterministic Verifier V interposing on every outbound tool call and external message release across agent trajectories (Section 3–4, pp. 4–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem SP-1 (Sound Budget Enforcement, p. 4) & Lemma 1 (Model-relative sub-additivity, p. 7): cumulative min-entropy leakage across a trajectory never exceeds the sink-trust-weighted budget B, even if the untrusted defender LLM is jailbroken (unverified atoms default to worst-case cost).
Trust_Assumptions: Deterministic Verifier V, versioned rubric library R, Merkle-chained ledger L, and signing key sk_V inside the host harness are trusted; neither the main agent LLM nor the local defender LLM is trusted for soundness (Section 3.2, p. 5).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on OCELOT-Traj-500 (5 seeds, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, Table 2 p. 10): achieves lowest cumulative min-entropy leakage and 0% budget exceedance with highest task utility against injection, jailbreak, cumulative inference, and 4-sink collusion at 18% wall-clock overhead (defender p50 = 142 ms, deterministic verifier p50 = 62 ms, p99 = 249 ms, Table 7 p. 13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Witness-Verified Declassification (WVD), credal posterior min-entropy budget accounting, and Merkle-chained signed leakage ledger.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Guarantee is relative to the calibrated rubric cost bounds (Bootstrap UCB coverage 96.6% vs 95% target, Table 4 p. 12) and pre-specified secret schema; verifier signing key sk_V uses classical signatures (STAGE_0).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1–2), Theorem SP-1 (p. 4), & Section 5.5 Table 7 (p. 13): "Because every unverified atom is costed at worst-case risk, a jailbroken defender yields conservative fallback, never silent leakage... at 18% wall-clock overhead (§5)... The defender pass dominates per-release latency (Table 7: 142ms at p50); the verifier adds 62ms at p50 and 249ms at p99."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: OCELOT enforces trajectory-wide posterior-risk privacy budgets via Witness-Verified Declassification and a Merkle-chained signed ledger (Theorem SP-1), resisting adaptive injection and multi-sink collusion at 18% wall-clock overhead (verifier p50 = 62 ms).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal soundness proofs (Theorem SP-1, Lemma 1) and 500-trajectory multi-seed evaluation across 4 adversarial regimes (18 pp.).
Protected_Object: User PII/secrets across multi-step outbound tool calls, external service releases, and per-trajectory leakage ledgers.

Study_Title: KedgeFlow: A Programmable Control Plane for Enterprise AI Agents

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Ed25519 digital signatures over restricted RFC 8785 canonical JSON envelopes (P || 0 || C(E^-)), lowercase hex SHA-256 digests of proposals/descriptors/grants, and atomic single-use execution root (rho) claims in a 3-node etcd store with monotonic fencing tokens.
Enforcement_Point_Location: KedgeFlow 3-Plane Architecture: Control Plane (Policy Authority, Resource Registry, Admission Controller, Grant Authority, Outcome Service) and Enforcement Plane (MCP Execution Gateway & Resource Adapter holding exclusive target mutation credentials, Figure 1, p. 2).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proposition 1 (Single-use authority: at most one successful claim per execution root allowance rho across replacement generations gamma, p. 9) and Proposition 2 (Exact-action dispatch binding: every governed dispatch matches its verified grant G, claimed allowance, and active policy/ownership epoch, p. 10).
Trust_Assumptions: Control Plane issuers, enrolled Ed25519 keys, 3-node etcd atomic authority store, Execution Gateway, credential broker, and target fencing guard are in the TCB; agent runtime holds zero direct target mutation credentials (Section 2.1, p. 2).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Single-resource MCP reference evaluation (Section 5, pp. 11–14): 6,560 concurrent ledger claim attempts across 82 allowances yielded exactly 1 successful claim per allowance (82 wins, 6,478 rejections); 12 deterministic boundary tests (Table 2, p. 14) rejected all altered/unauthorized calls before consumption; a 32-call gateway race produced 1 committed mock effect; lost-response retry produced 0 additional dispatches.
Exposed_Security_Function: MCP-facing Execution Gateway, Ed25519/RFC-8785 exact-action grant verifier, etcd atomic single-use root ledger, credential exchange broker, and Unknown-outcome retention.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly demonstrates (Table 2–3, pp. 14–15) that a deliberately permissive policy still authorizes an undesirable effect; distributed multi-resource reservations across distinct roots, native crash recovery, and real production target adapters remain untested; relies on classical Ed25519 (STAGE_0).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 4.1–4.2 (pp. 8–10): "Under trusted issuance of exact-action authority, two conditional properties establish at most one successful claim per allowance and link every governed dispatch to a matching grant, claim, and subsequent dispatch authorization, even when the agent is compromised... In the single-resource evaluation, 6,560 concurrent ledger claim attempts yielded exactly one successful claim for each of 82 allowances."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: KedgeFlow separates agent reasoning from execution authority via Ed25519/RFC-8785 exact-action grants, atomic single-use etcd root allowances, and fenced gateway dispatch, guaranteeing at-most-one claim per allowance (6,560 concurrent attempts -> 82/82 exact wins).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Conditional safety proofs (Propositions 1–2) and single-resource MCP gateway concurrency & boundary evaluation over 3-node etcd (18 pp.).
Protected_Object: Frozen action proposals q, signed execution grants G, single-use execution root allowances rho, target mutation credentials, and outcome receipts.
Composition_Evidence: Links admission & Ed25519 grant issuance (B2), atomic etcd root consumption & fenced target dispatch (B3), and retained outcome receipts/Unknown-state reconciliation (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Audit ulang baris pilot CLM-0034 dari PDF teks lengkap (18 hlm.). Memperbaiki locator seksi (Section 4 Propositions 1–2 hlm. 8–10; Section 5 Table 2–3 hlm. 11–15), merinci primitif kriptografi (Ed25519 + RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256 + etcd), dan menyelaraskan Boundary_Codes ke B2;B3;B4.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0034 telah diaudit ulang secara menyeluruh dari PDF teks lengkap 18 hlm. oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: AgentCrypt: Advancing Privacy and (Secure) Computation in AI Agent Collaboration
Threat_Attacker_Model: Post-access sensitive data leakage across multi-agent collaboration (14 attack/error classes including prompt injection, impersonation, multi-hop routing, unauthorized aggregation, tool misselection, and unintentional agent errors) under FERPA, HIPAA, GLBA, GDPR, and CCPA.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Three-level deterministic cryptographic wrapper: Identity-Based Encryption (IBE) for policy-bound encrypted retrieval (Level 2) and Secure Multiparty Computation (MPC) / Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) for blind computation over encrypted tags (Level 3, Table 1, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: AgentCrypt deterministic cryptographic wrapper integrated into LangGraph and Google ADK inter-agent communication and tool-execution channels (Section 3–4, pp. 3–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Formal worst-case cryptographic non-disclosure guarantee for policy-tagged sensitive data across single-hop and multi-hop agent routing, independent of LLM non-determinism or prompt injection.
Trust_Assumptions: All sensitive data fields are accurately tagged with privacy metadata in an offline phase before agent ingestion (explicitly stated p. 9; missing tags halt execution fail-closed in 120/120 tests, Table 3 p. 26); Key Authority and cryptographic primitives (IBE/MPC/FHE) are secure.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 914 privacy-annotated multi-agent scenarios spanning 14 attack/error classes and 5 regulations (Table 2, p. 9) plus 120 untagged-cell fail-closed tests (Table 3, p. 26): achieves 100% privacy preservation (0% leakage ASR across all 914 scenarios and 120 untagged probes) while maintaining 84%–98.6% task correctness.
Exposed_Security_Function: Three-level cryptographic data wrapper (Level 1 access gating, Level 2 IBE policy-bound decryption, Level 3 MPC/FHE secure computation) for LangGraph and Google ADK.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Depends critically on complete offline privacy-policy tagging of all sensitive data cells prior to runtime (Section 6, p. 9); Level 3 FHE/MPC computation incurs higher latency for complex non-linear analytics; classical pairing-based IBE is pre-quantum (STAGE_0).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Table 2 (p. 9): "The framework spans policy-based encrypted retrieval (Level 2, via identity-based encryption) and any computation (Level 3), with optional fully homomorphic encryption when raw data access must be eliminated... AgentCrypt maintains 84% task correctness while preserving privacy in 100% of the scenarios."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: AgentCrypt enforces worst-case multi-agent data privacy via a 3-level deterministic cryptographic wrapper (IBE and MPC/FHE) in LangGraph and Google ADK, achieving 100% privacy preservation and 84% task correctness across 914 scenarios.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal cryptographic security definitions and empirical evaluation across 914 multi-agent scenarios (14 classes) and 120 untagged-data probes (30 pp.).
Protected_Object: Policy-tagged sensitive data records (FERPA, HIPAA, GLBA, GDPR, CCPA) traversing multi-hop agent collaboration and computation.
Composition_Evidence: Preserves cryptographic data confidentiality across multi-hop agent-to-agent delegation (B2) and encrypted tool computation (B3) without trusting intermediate LLM agents.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (30 hlm.). Memvalidasi kerangka 3-level AgentCrypt (IBE + MPC/FHE) pada LangGraph dan Google ADK beserta evaluasi 914 skenario (Table 2 hlm. 9: 100% privasi, 84%–98.6% utilitas) dan 120 uji fail-closed (Table 3 hlm. 26).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 30 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
Threat_Attacker_Model: Automated red-teaming adversary using Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search (T-MAP) to evolve adversarial prompts that bypass LLM text guardrails and realize multi-step harmful tool executions (Level 3 trajectory realization) across MCP servers.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Trajectory-aware evolutionary search with 3-level execution trajectory fitness scoring, mutation/crossover operators, and diversity-preserving archive across 5 MCP environments).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Multi-step MCP tool-invocation loop evaluated across 5 MCP server environments and frontier LLMs (GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V3, Section 3–4, pp. 3–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that text-level safety alignment and refusal training fail to prevent multi-step harmful tool realization when guided by execution-trajectory feedback.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can submit user prompts or external content and observe or simulate agent tool-execution trajectories during evolutionary search.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 5 MCP server environments and frontier LLMs (Table 1–5, pp. 5–8), T-MAP substantially lowers Refusal Rate (RR) and increases Attack Realization Rate (ARR, up to 88% in ablation Table 4 p. 8) and unique cross-server trajectory diversity (Table 2 & Table 5, pp. 6, 8) compared to single-turn and text-only red-teaming baselines.
Exposed_Security_Function: T-MAP trajectory-aware evolutionary red-teaming framework and 3-level MCP execution harm rubric (https://github.com/pwnhyo/T-MAP).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated in sandboxed MCP environments covering 5 MCP servers without external cryptographic pre-action authorization gates or human-in-the-loop confirmation (explicitly noted in Limitations, p. 9).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Limitations (p. 9): "Empirical evaluations across diverse MCP environments demonstrate that T-MAP substantially outperforms baselines in attack realization rate (ARR) and remains effective against frontier models, including GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, and GLM-5... Our evaluation covers five MCP servers, while extending it to broader agent environments remains important future work."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: T-MAP uses trajectory-aware evolutionary search over multi-step MCP execution traces to maximize Attack Realization Rate (ARR) across 5 MCP environments against frontier models (GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, GLM-5).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Open-source red-teaming framework and empirical evaluation across 5 sandboxed MCP server environments and frontier LLMs (36 pp.).
Protected_Object: Multi-step MCP tool invocations (email, filesystem, browser/Playwright, financial APIs).
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates cross-server trajectory chaining (Table 5, p. 8) where benign-looking initial MCP tool calls (e.g., reading emails) compose into harmful downstream exfiltration or state mutation.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (36 hlm.). Memvalidasi metode serangan evolusioner berbasis trajektori T-MAP pada 5 lingkungan MCP terhadap model frontier (Tables 1–5 hlm. 5–8) serta kode sumber terbuka.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 36 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: A Five-Plane Reference Architecture for Runtime Governance of Production AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Seven production-agent systems threats (T1–T7, Section 3 & Table 1, p. 11): indirect prompt injection, confused-deputy delegation escalation, cross-step toxic capability composition, tool/connector overreach, session-state contamination, unverifiable partial audit trails, and stale/unrevoked delegated authority.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Macaroon-inspired cryptographic capability-attenuation chains binding composite principals (intersection of delegator capability sets and TTLs), stateful session-predicate adjudication, and hash-chained tamper-evident composed evidence records.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Five-Plane Reference Architecture: single Reasoning Plane adjudicating across 7 Mediation Points (MP1–MP7, Table 2 p. 22) with 6 interruption primitives (pause, escalate, narrow, modify, defer, rollback) projected onto 4 Enforcement Planes (Network, Identity, Endpoint, Data, Section 4–5, pp. 13–24).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Four structural correctness invariants (Sections 4–7): Invariant 1 (Composed Authority, p. 16), Invariant 2 (Mediation Coverage across MP1–MP7, p. 24), Invariant 3 (Bounded Composite Authority via monotonic capability-lattice intersection), and Invariant 4 (Evidence Sufficiency & partial-log reconstructability).
Trust_Assumptions: Reasoning plane policy adjudicator, identity provider issuing base principal capabilities, and the 4 infrastructure enforcement planes (service mesh, IAM, sandbox, DLP) fail-closed unless all applicable plane directives succeed.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Policy-engine core reference implementation evaluated over 20,000 iterations on a 32-clause policy across delegation-chain lengths 1–16 (Section 8.5, Table 5, pp. 53–54): mean per-decision adjudication latency is 5–15 us (p99 < 20 us), with 100% attenuation correctness and 100% audit tamper-evidence reconstructability.
Exposed_Security_Function: Composite-principal capability-attenuation adjudicator, 7-point stop-anywhere mediation (pause/escalate/narrow/modify/defer/rollback), 4-plane directive projection, and reconstructible audit substrate.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly states (Abstract p. 1, Section 11 p. 56) that the four invariants are argued structurally rather than mechanically proved, and empirical measurements validate the policy-engine core microbenchmark (5–15 us) while full end-to-end live-agent evaluation on AgentDojo (Section 10) is left as future work.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 8.5 Table 5 (pp. 53–54): "A reference implementation of the policy-engine core supplies measured evidence: attenuation correctness and evidence reconstructability hold on every trial, adjudication runs in single-digit microseconds, and the audit substrate's tamper-evidence behaves exactly as designed... Adjudication latency, mean (chain length 1–16): 5–15 us; 99th percentile < 20 us."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Presents a five-plane reference architecture (Reasoning + Network, Identity, Endpoint, Data) with 7 mediation points, 6 interruption primitives, composite-principal capability attenuation, and reconstructible audit, achieving 5–15 us mean adjudication latency (p99 < 20 us).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 62-page reference architecture, 4 structural invariants, 5 domain workflow case studies, and policy-engine core microbenchmarks (20,000 trials, chain length 1–16).
Protected_Object: Composite principal delegation chains, multi-step action plans, enterprise systems of record across 4 infrastructure planes, and composed audit evidence records.
Composition_Evidence: Formally defines capability-set lattice intersection along multi-hop delegation chains (B1/B2), projects decisions across 4 enforcement planes (B3), and binds all plane realizations into a single hash-chained evidence record (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Audit ulang baris pilot CLM-0035 dari PDF teks lengkap (62 hlm.). TEMUAN AUDIT: Baris pilot mengkodekan Implementation_Maturity = CONCEPTUAL_ARCHITECTURE dan mengutip hlm. 41, padahal PDF memiliki 62 halaman dan melaporkan implementasi referensi inti mesin kebijakan pada Section 8.5 / Table 5 (hlm. 53–54) dengan latensi 5–15 us (p99 < 20 us) pada 20.000 iterasi. Diperbarui ke RESEARCH_PROTOTYPE_SIMULATOR dengan kutipan dan metrik eksak.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0035 telah diaudit ulang dari PDF teks lengkap 62 hlm. oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: RAS-Eval: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Security Evaluation of LLM Agents in Real-World Environments
Threat_Attacker_Model: 3,802 attack tasks across 80 real-world and simulated test cases mapped to 11 CWE categories (including CWE-78 OS Command Injection, CWE-89 SQL Injection, CWE-22 Path Traversal, CWE-94 Code Injection, CWE-434 Unrestricted File Upload, CWE-79 XSS) targeting tool-augmented LLM agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (RAS-Eval security benchmark suite supporting dual Simulated and Real-World execution modes across JSON, LangGraph, and Model Context Protocol MCP tool formats).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent tool-invocation boundary across 80 test cases and 3 tool formats (JSON, LangGraph, MCP) evaluated on 6 SOTA LLMs (Section 2–4, pp. 2–10).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies real-world vs. simulated CWE vulnerability exposure and task completion degradation across LLM agent architectures and tool protocols.
Trust_Assumptions: Containerized real-execution and simulated-execution environments accurately measure Task Completion Rate (TCR) and Attack Success Rate (ASR) across 3,802 tasks.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 6 SOTA LLMs on 80 test cases and 3,802 attack tasks (Abstract p. 1, Section 4 pp. 6–10): attacks reduced agent Task Completion Rate (TCR) by 36.78% on average and achieved up to 85.65% Attack Success Rate (ASR) in academic scenarios; larger models demonstrated lower ASR than smaller models within the same family.
Exposed_Security_Function: RAS-Eval benchmark (80 test cases, 3,802 attack tasks, 11 CWEs, JSON/LangGraph/MCP dual-mode execution harness, https://github.com/lanzer-tree/RAS-Eval).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Diagnostic benchmark paper that exposes high baseline CWE vulnerability (up to 85.65% ASR) in undefended JSON/LangGraph/MCP agents rather than proposing a new cryptographic or runtime enforcement mechanism.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "RAS-Eval comprises 80 test cases and 3,802 attack tasks mapped to 11 Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) categories, with tools implemented in JSON, LangGraph, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) formats. We evaluate 6 state-of-the-art LLMs across diverse scenarios, revealing significant vulnerabilities: attacks reduced agent task completion rates (TCR) by 36.78% on average and achieved an 85.65% success rate in academic settings."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: RAS-Eval benchmarks 6 SOTA LLMs across 80 test cases and 3,802 attack tasks mapped to 11 CWEs in JSON, LangGraph, and MCP formats, showing a 36.78% average TCR drop and up to 85.65% ASR.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Open-source dual-mode benchmark evaluation across 3,802 attack tasks, 11 CWEs, 3 tool protocols, and 6 LLMs (12 pp.).
Protected_Object: Host OS, filesystem, database, and web service interfaces invoked via JSON, LangGraph, and MCP tools.
Composition_Evidence: Compares vulnerability exposure across JSON, LangGraph, and MCP tool-execution interfaces under both simulated in-memory and real containerized execution.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (12 hlm.). Memvalidasi benchmark RAS-Eval (80 kasus uji, 3.802 tugas serangan, 11 CWE, format JSON/LangGraph/MCP) dengan penurunan TCR rata-rata 36.78% dan ASR hingga 85.65%.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 12 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture
Threat_Attacker_Model: Key exfiltration from software-accessible memory/env vars and confused-deputy signing attacks (via indirect prompt injection in AgentDojo or compromised MCP server tool poisoning in MCPTox) coercing an agent into signing unauthorized Git commits, documents, or release artifacts.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Hardware Keystore confinement (PKCS#11 SoftHSMv2 and embedded TPM 2.0 non-extractable private keys) paired with a 5-layer Zero-Trust MCP enforcement stack: manifest tool allowlisting, SHA-256 pre-committed payload hash binding, local air-gapped Runtime Alignment Validator (RAV), human-in-the-loop escalation, and PKCS#11 hardware signing.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Kernel & PKCS#11/TPM 2.0 Hardware Keystore boundary interposing between the LLM agent and cryptographic signing operations (Section 3–4, pp. 3–7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Zero private-key extractability from host RAM/filesystem and 0% unauthorized signing Attack Success Rate (ASR) when operator intent is pre-committed via SHA-256 payload hashes or gated by human confirmation.
Trust_Assumptions: Hardware keystore (TPM 2.0 / HSM) preserves key non-extractability; MCP enforcement kernel sits outside the LLM process; human operator verifies escalated un-precommitted signing prompts.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on AgentDojo keystore benchmark across 4 models (n=144 combined trials) and MCPTox tool poisoning: reduces prompt-injection signing ASR from 18.1% baseline to 0% under the full 5-layer stack; deterministic manifest and SHA-256 payload-hash mismatches are rejected in <1 ms without LLM inference (Abstract p. 1, Section 4–5 pp. 4–10).
Exposed_Security_Function: 5-layer Zero-Trust MCP hardware signing stack with PKCS#11/TPM 2.0 non-extractable keys, SHA-256 intent hash pre-commitment, and HITL escalation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: When no payload hash can be pre-committed before an autonomous workflow, security falls back to human-in-the-loop approval because the LLM semantic filter (RAV) is defeated 100% of the time by adversarially plausible substitute filenames; PKCS#11/TPM 2.0 keys tested use classical algorithms (STAGE_0).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1–2) & Section 3 (pp. 4–5): "Prompt injection in content the agent reads (AgentDojo, three injection-following models, n=144) falls from an 18.1% baseline attack success rate to 0% under the full stack... If sign_payload is later called with a different payload, the kernel rejects it deterministically in <1 ms without LLM inference."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Combines PKCS#11/TPM 2.0 hardware keystores with a 5-layer Zero-Trust MCP enforcement stack (manifest check, <1 ms SHA-256 payload pre-commitment, RAV judge, HITL gate), reducing AgentDojo signing ASR from 18.1% to 0% (n=144).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Hardware-keystore MCP prototype validated on SoftHSMv2 and TPM 2.0 across AgentDojo (n=144) and MCPTox benchmarks (15 pp.).
Protected_Object: Operator private signing keys (Git commits, documents, release artifacts) and MCP sign_payload invocations.
Composition_Evidence: Binds operator pre-committed SHA-256 payload intent (B1) across MCP tool discovery/poisoning defenses (B2) to PKCS#11/TPM 2.0 hardware signing execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (15 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur 5-lapis Zero-Trust MCP dengan PKCS#11 SoftHSMv2 & TPM 2.0, penurunan ASR dari 18.1% ke 0% (n=144), dan penolakan deterministik <1 ms.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 15 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial filename substitution probe targeting the LLM-based Runtime Alignment Validator (RAV, local air-gapped atla/selene-mini:q4_k_m) when no cryptographic payload hash was pre-committed by the operator.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Adversarially plausible substitute document naming that mimics operator task semantics to bypass semantic LLM-as-a-judge alignment filters).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Layer 3 Runtime Alignment Validator (RAV) semantic LLM filter in the MCP signing pipeline (Abstract p. 2, Section 5, pp. 9–11).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves empirically that semantic LLM alignment filters cannot serve as a standalone trust boundary against confused-deputy signing attacks.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can name or inject a malicious payload under a task-plausible filename within the agent's workspace.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: While the RAV semantic filter detects 100% of substitute documents bearing unrelated names, an adversarially plausible substitute name defeats the semantic filter in 100% of trials (0% RAV detection rate), requiring Layer 2 SHA-256 pre-commitment or Layer 4 human-in-the-loop escalation to block (Abstract p. 2, Section 5 pp. 9–11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Adversarial semantic-substitution probe evaluating the boundary of LLM-judge alignment filters in hardware-signing workflows.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates a fundamental limitation of semantic LLM judges (atla/selene-mini) when evaluating un-precommitted autonomous signing requests.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 2): "A further probe delineates exactly how far the semantic filter's protection extends: it detects a substitute document under an unrelated name, but an adversarially plausible substitute name defeats it completely, in every trial we ran. We report this as a central finding, not a caveat: the architecture's guarantee never rests on the filter being right, only on a human being asked whenever no hash was pre-committed."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An adversarially plausible substitute document name defeats the local LLM Runtime Alignment Validator (atla/selene-mini) in 100% of trials, proving that signing guarantees must rest on SHA-256 pre-commitment or human confirmation rather than semantic filters.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled adversarial probe of the Layer 3 RAV semantic filter across plausible vs. unrelated filename substitutions (15 pp.).
Protected_Object: Semantic alignment judgment between operator task intent and un-precommitted signing payloads.
Composition_Evidence: Shows why cryptographic hash pre-commitment (Layer 2) and HITL confirmation (Layer 4) are strictly necessary to close the semantic gap left by LLM judges (Layer 3).
Coding_Rationale: Dekomposisi klaim sekunder (CLM-E06-020B) untuk merekam temuan sentral penulis bahwa filter semantik LLM (RAV) gagal 100% terhadap nama berkas substitusi yang masuk akal secara kontekstual.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 15 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: From Review to Authorization: Key-Isolated Threshold Signing for LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection or compromise of the LLM proposer agent and up to t-1 reviewer-signer domains attempting to forge an authorization signature, mutate canonical action parameters, or replay approvals for high-consequence actions (payments, permission changes).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: t-of-n Threshold BLS signatures (over BLS12-381 via py_ecc) with key shares isolated outside all LLM processes, bound to a canonical authorization object (domain separator, schema version, principal/committee/epoch IDs, action digest, expiry, Table 1, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: KITA (Key-Isolated Threshold Authorization) Reviewer-to-Executor boundary: structured-output LLM reviewer adapter, authenticated approval gate, isolated threshold BLS share signers, combiner, and exact-action executor verifier (Section 2–4, pp. 2–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Execution-bound authorization integrity under threshold BLS EUF-CMA unforgeability: compromising the LLM proposer and fewer than t reviewer-signer domains cannot produce a valid signature for a new or altered canonical action without at least one uncompromised domain's approved share.
Trust_Assumptions: At least n - t + 1 reviewer-signer domains remain uncompromised; threshold BLS signing key shares reside outside LLM processes; correlated LLM reviewer failures (latent correlation rho) are bounded by quorum sizing t (Table 6, p. 13).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Validated across 6 deterministic end-to-end system tests (Table 5, p. 13: quorum gating, message mutation rejection, epoch/replay rejection) and Python py_ecc threshold BLS microbenchmarks (p. 14: for (n=3, t=2), share sign ~4.8 ms, share verify ~9.2 ms, combine ~0.3 ms, final verify ~11.1 ms) plus correlated failure threshold sweeps (n=7, rho=0..0.45, Table 6 p. 13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Key-isolated t-of-n threshold BLS signing over canonical action objects with correlated-reviewer quorum sizing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Correlated LLM reasoning failures across homogeneous model reviewers (high latent correlation rho) can still approve a malicious action if t LLM reviewers are tricked simultaneously (analyzed in Table 6, p. 13); pairing-based BLS12-381 is pre-quantum (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 6 (pp. 13–14, Tables 5–6): "We present KITA, a review-to-authorization architecture that keeps the user's personal secret signing key and every threshold signing-key share outside all LLM processes. Under threshold-signature unforgeability and our system assumptions, compromising the proposer and fewer than t reviewer–signer domains cannot produce a valid authorization for a new action... Six system tests validate quorum gating and message binding at this interface, while cryptographic microbenchmarks measure the online signing path."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: KITA isolates t-of-n threshold BLS signing shares outside all LLM processes and binds signatures to canonical action objects, preventing a compromised proposer and <t reviewer domains from forging execution authorization.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Threshold BLS security reduction, correlated-failure statistical model (Table 6), 6 system tests (Table 5), and py_ecc microbenchmarks (14 pp.).
Protected_Object: Threshold BLS key shares, canonical authorization objects (Table 1), and high-consequence tool executions (payments, permission changes).
Composition_Evidence: Separates untrusted LLM proposal generation (B1) from multi-domain reviewer approval & key-isolated threshold BLS share combination (B2) and exact-action verifier execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur KITA berbasis threshold BLS (t-of-n key isolation di luar proses LLM), 6 pengujian sistem (Table 5 hlm. 13), pemodelan korelasi kegagalan reviewer rho (Table 6 hlm. 13), dan mikrobenchmark py_ecc (hlm. 14).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 14 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: OpenClaw PRISM: A Zero-Fork, Defense-in-Depth Runtime Security Layer for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-stage runtime attacks on OpenClaw tool-augmented LLM gateways, including indirect prompt injection via fetched web/tool content, unsafe shell/filesystem/network tool execution, outbound credential/secret leakage, sub-agent privilege escalation, and tampering with local control files or audit logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Chained SHA-256 hash linkage and HMAC-based integrity protection with periodic anchors over audit logs (Section 4.5, p. 8), paired with a 10-hook zero-fork plugin, 4 sidecar services, and TTL-decayed session risk accumulation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: OpenClaw PRISM in-process plugin across 10 lifecycle hooks (message ingress, prompt construction, tool call, tool result, outbound message, sub-agent spawn, startup) and 4 sidecars (heuristic/LLM scanner, policy engine, file watcher, audit service, Table 1, p. 9).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Defense-in-depth runtime policy containment across tools, paths, private networks, and outbound secrets, plus post-hoc detection of audit log tampering via HMAC and hash-chain verification (Case 6, p. 17).

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly notes (p. 17 & Section 8 p. 21) that HMAC/hash-chain audit log protection is post-hoc detective rather than preventive if host storage is modified, local LLM sidecar scanning introduces high latency, and current evaluation is a preliminary 80-case curated slice.

Threat_Attacker_Model: Software supply chain attacks across SDLC stages (malicious commits, vulnerable dependencies/SBOMs, CI/CD misconfigurations, tampered build artifacts) as well as rogue/impersonated security monitoring agents or forged security attestations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Consortium Certificate Authority (PKI/TLS), per-agent cryptographic digital signatures (Sign_sk_a(h_l)), SHA-256 report hashes (h_l = SHA256(R_l)), and a permissioned PoA/BFT blockchain executing Agent Registry, Attestation Log, and Release-Policy smart contracts.
Enforcement_Point_Location: AttestChain multi-agent SDLC security layer (Source, Dependency/SBOM, CI Config, Artifact, and Runtime Policy agents) and permissioned blockchain Release-Policy smart contract gating CI/CD deployment (Sections 4–6, pp. 10–20).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Authenticated agent identity (via Consortium CA + on-chain Agent Registry), non-repudiable tamper-evident security attestations (SHA-256 + digital signature), and deterministic smart-contract release gating.
Trust_Assumptions: Consortium CA, permissioned PoA/BFT blockchain consensus nodes, and agent private signing keys sk_a remain uncompromised; LLM agents do not directly mutate production systems (explicitly stated p. 10).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated in a resource-optimized and energy-aware SDLC testbed (Section 7, pp. 21–24): on-chain anchoring stores only 32-byte SHA-256 report digests and signatures (keeping off-chain full JSON reports) under lightweight PoA/BFT consensus to minimize energy and storage overhead while gating releases.
Exposed_Security_Function: 5 specialized SDLC security agents, Consortium CA identity binding, SHA-256 signed attestation generation, and on-chain Release-Policy smart contract enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Inherits LLM inference latency and potential semantic false positives/negatives during report generation (Section 8, p. 24); relies on pre-quantum PKI/digital signatures (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).

A proof-of-authority (PoA) or Byzantine fault-tolerant (BFT-style) consensus mechanism is assumed."

Study_Title: Overlaying Governance: A Compositional Authorization Framework for Delegation and Scope in Agentic AI
Threat_Attacker_Model: Overly permissive agent authority, recursive sub-agent delegation escalation, out-of-scope resource access, and prompt-injection-induced unauthorized actions across multi-agent MCP/A2A ecosystems where static OAuth 2.0 scopes fail (Section 1–2, pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Relational Compositional Governance Operator overlaying 6 contractual delegation types—full, scoped with attenuation, conditional, depth-bounded K, temporal, group n-of-m—and dynamic resource scope envelopes onto Google Zanzibar / OpenFGA ReBAC multigraphs).
Enforcement_Point_Location: OpenFGA / Zanzibar ReBAC Policy Decision Point (PDP) and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) evaluating the composed authorization graph G = (V, E) with contextual edge conditions Gamma at every agent resource request (Section 3–4, pp. 3–9).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Lemma 5.1 (Conservative extension for human domain principals, p. 10), Lemma 5.2 (Human-rooted delegation chain invariant, p. 10), and Theorem 5.3 (Agent-authorization soundness: an agent is authorized iff connected to a permitted human root via an active, scope-attenuated, condition-satisfied delegation chain, p. 10).
Trust_Assumptions: OpenFGA/Zanzibar ReBAC relation graph is acyclic and well-founded; PEP mediates all agent resource accesses and supplies authentic runtime context ctx (time, network, session).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on OpenFGA across Google Drive and Slack domain models and large synthetic ReBAC graphs (Section 5.2, pp. 11–13, Table 1; code at https://github.com/Amjad-Ibrahim-Huawei/compositional-paper): median authorization check latency remains <7 ms across overlay delegation depths and graph scales.
Exposed_Security_Function: Compositional ReBAC overlay operator, 6 contractual delegation primitives, hierarchical resource scope envelope attenuation, and OpenFGA runtime check evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Semantic ordering for scope attenuation remains domain-specific and must be defined in the container/scope hierarchy by policy designers (explicitly noted Section 3.2, p. 4); does not specify cryptographic token formats for cross-organization transport.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1), Section 5.1 (p. 10, Lemmas 5.1–5.2), & Section 5.2 (p. 13): "To operationalize this composition, we define a compositional operator that overlays new agentic semantics, such as recursive delegation chains, onto existing relational policies without rewriting them. We substantiate this framework through formal proofs and empirical evaluation... median check times remain under 7 ms even without specialized optimization."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Formalizes a compositional ReBAC governance overlay on OpenFGA/Zanzibar supporting 6 contractual agentic delegation types and scope-attenuated envelopes with soundness proofs (Lemmas 5.1–5.2) and <7 ms median check latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal userset algebra proofs (Lemmas 5.1–5.2) and OpenFGA empirical benchmarks across Google Drive, Slack, and synthetic ReBAC graphs (15 pp.).

Memperbarui Implementation_Maturity ke OPEN_SOURCE_COMMIT (repo GitHub Huawei tersedia pada catatan kaki 2 hlm. 2), merinci bukti Lemma 5.1–5.2 (hlm. 10) dan latensi median <7 ms pada OpenFGA (hlm. 13), serta menyelaraskan Boundary_Codes ke B1;B2;B4.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0036 telah diaudit ulang secara menyeluruh dari PDF teks lengkap 15 hlm. oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Beyond Max Tokens: Stealthy Resource Amplification via Tool Calling Chains in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious or compromised third-party MCP server executing a stealthy, multi-turn economic Denial-of-Service (DoS) / resource amplification attack by editing text-visible tool metadata fields and applying a template-driven return policy optimized via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) while preserving task completion.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (MCTS-optimized text-visible MCP tool metadata edits and multi-turn template-driven calibration response policy inducing verbose tool-calling chains).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent–MCP tool interaction loop (tool registration metadata and multi-turn tool response ingestion) evaluated across 6 LLMs on ToolBench and BFCL (Section 3–4, pp. 2–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that preserving function signatures and terminal benign payloads allows a malicious MCP server to bypass prompt filters and output monitors while causing up to 658x token/financial cost amplification.
Trust_Assumptions: Agent connects to an attacker-controlled MCP server and allows multi-turn tool calling up to standard framework step/token limits.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 6 LLMs on ToolBench and BFCL (Abstract p. 1, Section 4 pp. 6–8): induces multi-turn trajectories exceeding 60,000 tokens, increases per-query financial/token cost by up to 658x, increases GPU energy consumption by 100–560x, and drives GPU KV-cache occupancy to 35%–74% while maintaining benign-equivalent Task Success Rate (TSR).
Exposed_Security_Function: MCTS-optimized multi-turn MCP tool-calling chain resource amplification attack benchmark.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated in a controlled agent emulator with deterministic stubbed tool payloads on single-tool subsets of ToolBench/BFCL (explicitly noted in Limitations, p. 9); structured numeric calibration sequences may be detectable by per-tool call-count or token-budget circuit breakers.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "Across six LLMs on ToolBench and BFCL benchmarks, our attack yields trajectories over 60K tokens, increases per-query cost by up to 658x, raises energy by 100–560x, and pushes GPU key-value (KV) cache occupancy to 35–74%. Standard prompt filters and output trajectory monitors seldom detect these attacks."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCTS-optimized MCP tool metadata edits and template-driven return policies steer LLM agents into >60K-token tool-calling chains across 6 LLMs on ToolBench and BFCL, amplifying per-query cost up to 658x and energy by 100–560x while preserving task success.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark evaluation of multi-turn MCP resource amplification across 6 LLMs on ToolBench and BFCL (14 pp.).
Protected_Object: LLM agent token budgets, GPU KV-cache memory, energy consumption, and MCP tool-calling loop termination.
Composition_Evidence: Combines text-only MCP tool description manipulation at discovery/registration (B2) with multi-turn template-driven tool-response chaining during execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm.) dan resolusi status UNMAPPED pada register menjadi MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3). Memvalidasi serangan amplifikasi sumber daya multi-turn MCP (>60K token, biaya hingga 658x, energi 100–560x, KV-cache 35–74% pada 6 LLM di ToolBench & BFCL).
