Study_Title: Ghost in the Context: Policy-Carriage Integrity in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Context-window pressure and workload-content flooding by external content providers causing eviction, truncation, summarization weakening, or unbinding of active trusted system policies during context assembly in AutoGen/tau3 and OpenHands/SWE-bench agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (ControlCapsule reference design pattern: typed policy provenance tags, isolated control-plane token budget B_effective = W_backend - T_fixed - T_reserved, preflight fit verification, fail-closed overload handling, and action-boundary policy enforcement).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Agent Context Assembler (ControlCapsule) and pre-action structured policy enforcement gate before model invocation and tool dispatch (Section III–IV, pp. 3–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Policy-Carriage Integrity: 100% of applicable trusted policies remain present, exact (unweakened/unsummarized), and bound in the assembled decision state across context-pressure sweeps, or assembly fails closed.
Trust_Assumptions: Host context assembler and scheduler implementation are trusted and not controlled by external content providers (Section II, p. 2).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Controlled pressure replay over AutoGen/tau3 and OpenHands/SWE-bench traces (168 traces per configuration, Tables III–XIII, pp. 6–19): protected-placement configurations (Policy-last replay, Constraint-aware ControlCapsule) achieve 100.0% policy-carriage preservation and 0.0% absent/non-equivalent policy degradation vs 23.8%–28.6% loss in task-local/recency baselines; fixed-assembler behavioral calibration yielded 0/90 unsafe proposals.
Exposed_Security_Function: ControlCapsule context-assembly budget isolator, preflight policy-fit verifier, fail-closed overload handler, and exact active-policy replay.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly keeps the primary guarantee state-level (preserving policy presence in the context window) rather than behavioral: even when policy is present in context, an LLM can still misinterpret it unless paired with deterministic action-boundary enforcement (Abstract p. 1).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Table XIII (p. 19): "We study policy-carriage integrity: applicable trusted policies must remain present, sound, and correctly bound in the decision state immediately before action. Under controlled pressure replay over AutoGen/tau3 and OpenHands/SWE-bench traces, the tested protected-placement configurations preserve policy across the pressure sweep... We present CONTROLCAPSULE as a reference design pattern for these requirements."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ControlCapsule enforces policy-carriage integrity by isolating control-plane token budgets, preflight-checking active policy fit, and failing closed on context overload across AutoGen/tau3 and OpenHands/SWE-bench traces.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal context-budget model and controlled pressure-replay evaluation across 168-trace AutoGen/tau3 and OpenHands/SWE-bench suites (19 pp.).
Protected_Object: Active trusted system policies and control-plane token budgets during LLM context assembly.
Composition_Evidence: Preserves system/user policy state from initial prompt assembly (B1) through multi-turn tool/sub-agent context compaction (B2) to pre-action audit logging (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (19 hlm.). Memvalidasi konsep Policy-Carriage Integrity dan pola desain ControlCapsule pada replay AutoGen/tau3 dan OpenHands/SWE-bench (Tables III–XIII hlm. 6–19: 100.0% preservasi kebijakan vs 23.8%–28.6% degradasi pada baseline).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 19 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Firewalls to Secure Dynamic LLM Agentic Networks
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted or malicious external peer agents in dynamic agent-to-agent (A2A) networks using persuasive framing, urgency tactics, social engineering, or embedded prompt injections to exfiltrate user PII (privacy attacks) or hijack assistant tool execution (security attacks).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Dual-Firewall Task-Context Projection Architecture: incoming Language Converter Firewall projecting free-form peer messages onto a closed, deterministically verified domain-specific structured schema + outgoing Data Abstraction Firewall projecting user data onto minimum task-required granularity).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Trusted Dual-Firewall Mediation Layer (Language Converter Firewall on ingress + Data Abstraction Firewall on egress) isolating the user's assistant agent from external peer agents (Section 3–4, pp. 4–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Structural elimination of unconstrained natural-language injection channels on ingress and task-scoped data minimization on egress across dynamic multi-turn agent-to-agent negotiations.
Trust_Assumptions: Both firewalls execute in a trusted environment isolated from external peer input; domain-specific firewall rules learned from benign demonstrations cover valid task semantics (Section 3, p. 4).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 864 multi-turn attack episodes spanning 3 domains on the ConVerse benchmark (published in TMLR 06/2026, Abstract p. 1, Section 5 pp. 8–14): reduces Privacy ASR from 84% to 10% (and down to 7.51% in specific settings) and Security ASR from 60% to 3% on GPT-5 while maintaining or improving task completion utility.
Exposed_Security_Function: Language Converter Firewall (closed-schema ingress projection), Data Abstraction Firewall (egress granularity projection), and ConVerse 864-attack multi-agent benchmark.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Leaves a residual 10% privacy ASR and 3% security ASR when attackers exploit legitimate fields within the allowed task schema; requires learning or specifying domain-specific closed schemas for each task family.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "The Language Converter Firewall projects incoming messages onto a closed, domain-specific, structured protocol... The Data Abstraction Firewall projects outgoing information onto the granularity appropriate for the task... Across 864 attacks spanning three domains on the ConVerse benchmark, our architecture reduces privacy attack success rates (e.g., from 84% to 10% for GPT-5) and security attacks (from 60% to 3%), while maintaining or even improving task completion quality."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Introduces a dual-firewall architecture (Language Converter Firewall and Data Abstraction Firewall) for dynamic agentic networks, reducing privacy ASR from 84% to 10% and security ASR from 60% to 3% across 864 attacks on the ConVerse benchmark.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Peer-reviewed TMLR (06/2026) dual-firewall architecture and 864-attack multi-turn evaluation on the ConVerse benchmark (32 pp.).
Protected_Object: Incoming external agent messages (A2A ingress) and outgoing user private data (A2A egress).
Composition_Evidence: Mediates bidirectional multi-turn horizontal agent-to-agent negotiation (B2) and prevents downstream assistant tool hijacking (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (32 hlm., dipublikasikan di TMLR 06/2026). Memvalidasi arsitektur Dual-Firewall (Language Converter + Data Abstraction) dan hasil evaluasi pada 864 serangan di benchmark ConVerse (Privacy ASR 84% -> 10%, Security ASR 60% -> 3%).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 32 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: APPA: Recoverable Information-Flow Control for Real-World LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection, data exfiltration, and confused-deputy attacks across untrusted web/tool outputs where conventional monotone Information-Flow Control (IFC) taint tracking either over-blocks benign workflows or permanently strands contaminated agent trajectories.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (APPA — Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra: dual-phase reference monitor over composite security lattices with gradual security typing, bounded cast resolution, and disposable child-branch trajectory confinement exiting via shape-bounded attest-schema channels).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Dual-phase Reference Monitor at tool dispatch and MCP protocol gateways (prospective pre-execution label/history evaluation + post-execution output validation and on-demand child branch confinement, Section 3–4, pp. 3–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proposition 1 (Collapse, p. 4), Proposition 2 (Monotone descent and settlement, p. 4), Proposition 3 (No-laundering for gradual casts, p. 13), Theorem 6 (No unruled inadequate release, p. 14), and Corollary 7 (Recovery containment against prompt-injected models, p. 14).
Trust_Assumptions: APPA reference monitor and MCP gateway enforce label transitions and shape-bounded attest-schema branch exits outside the untrusted LLM's control.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 6,600 controlled benchmark episodes spanning OWASP AgentThreatBench and Bench-Corp enterprise workflows (Abstract p. 1, Table 1 p. 9): sustains 64.2%–91.0% task utility with 0.0% Attack Success Rate (0 observed attacks across all 1,320 guarded adversarial episodes, vs up to 48.2% unguarded ASR).
Exposed_Security_Function: Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra (APPA) dual-phase IFC reference monitor, gradual security typing casts, and disposable child-branch trajectory confinement (https://openappa.com).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Shape-bounded attest-schema channels restrict child-branch return types to finite/structured schemas; gradual typing casts require administrator-defined policy rules to prevent over-permissive declassification.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Appendix Proofs (pp. 13–14): "We prove core safety invariants: no-laundering gradual resolution, branch boundary isolation, and recovery containment against prompt-injected models. Across 6,600 controlled benchmark episodes spanning OWASP AgentThreatBench and enterprise workflows (Bench-Corp), APPA sustains 64.2–91% utility with zero observed attacks across 1,320 guarded episodes."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: APPA enforces recoverable Information-Flow Control via a dual-phase MCP reference monitor, gradual typing, and disposable child-branch confinement, proving safety invariants (Propositions 1–3, Theorem 6) and achieving 0% ASR across 1,320 guarded episodes (6,600 total episodes) with 64.2%–91% utility.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal lattice/type-soundness proofs (Propositions 1–3, Theorem 6, Corollary 7) and 6,600-episode benchmark evaluation on OWASP AgentThreatBench and Bench-Corp (22 pp.).
Protected_Object: Private context labels, untrusted tool/web outputs, child-branch execution states, and external side-effect sinks.

Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (22 hlm.). Memvalidasi bukti formal APPA (Propositions 1–3, Theorem 6, Corollary 7 hlm. 4, 13–14) dan evaluasi 6.600 episode (0% ASR pada 1.320 episode serangan terjaga, utilitas 64.2%–91%, Table 1 hlm. 9).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 22 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: MemLineage: Lineage-Guided Enforcement for LLM Agent Memory
Threat_Attacker_Model: Persistent memory poisoning and sleeper-via-derivation attacks where untrusted external content is summarized or laundered by an authentic principal into long-term agent memory and later retrieved to justify privileged tool invocations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: RFC-6962 Certificate Transparency-style Merkle log over per-principal Ed25519-signed memory entries combined with a weighted derivation DAG and max-of-strong-edges taint propagation rule.
Enforcement_Point_Location: MemLineage 6-module memory custody layer and Sensitive-Action Gate interposing between persistent memory retrieval, derivation writing, and privileged tool dispatch (Section 3–4, pp. 4–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 (Untrusted-Path Persistence, p. 6 & p. 21): any memory entry derived along a chain whose attribution edges remain above threshold tau preserves its external-ancestor taint label, and the sensitive-action gate deterministically refuses dispatches justified by external ancestors.
Trust_Assumptions: Host trusted computing base protects principal Ed25519 private keys and the RFC-6962 Merkle log root anchor (p. 5); derivation edge weights accurately capture semantic influence above threshold tau (conditional premise of Theorem 1, p. 7).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Drives Attack Success Rate (ASR) to 0.0% across all 3 memory-poisoning workloads in the deterministic mechanism-isolation harness and reduces strict AgentDojo banking ASR from 100% (6/6 failures on no-defense and signature-only baselines) to 0.0% with sub-millisecond (<1 ms) per-operation cryptographic/graph overhead (Abstract p. 1, Section 6–7 pp. 10–16).
Exposed_Security_Function: RFC-6962 Merkle log over Ed25519-signed memory entries, weighted derivation DAG tracker, and lineage-guided sensitive-action gate.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 8 (p. 3, p. 21) explicitly notes three limitations: Theorem 1 is conditional on attribution edge weights exceeding threshold tau, the strongest attribution algorithm requires white-box attention access, and Ed25519 signatures are pre-quantum (STAGE_0).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 4 Theorem 1 (p. 6): "It is a six-module design around an RFC-6962 Merkle log over per-principal Ed25519-signed entries: a weighted derivation DAG records which retrieved entries influenced each new memory, and a max-of-strong-edges propagation rule makes Untrusted-Path Persistence hold... MemLineage is the only configuration in that harness that drives all three columns to zero ASR, while sub-millisecond per-operation overhead keeps it well below the noise floor of any LLM call."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MemLineage combines an RFC-6962 Merkle log of Ed25519-signed memory entries with a weighted derivation DAG (Theorem 1 Untrusted-Path Persistence) to block sleeper-via-derivation memory attacks, achieving 0% ASR on AgentDojo banking and <1 ms per-operation overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal lineage persistence proof (Theorem 1), CI-verified deterministic harness, and AgentDojo banking evaluation (24 pp.).
Protected_Object: Long-term agent memory entries, derivation lineage DAGs, RFC-6962 Merkle log roots, and sensitive tool dispatches.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates why signature-only provenance fails under LLM summarization laundering (6/6 banking failures) and closes the gap by composing Ed25519/Merkle origin provenance (B1/B4) with derivation DAG gating at tool dispatch (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (24 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur MemLineage (RFC-6962 Merkle log + Ed25519 + derivation DAG), bukti Theorem 1 (hlm. 6 & 21), serta hasil 0% ASR dengan overhead <1 ms.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 24 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-party browser attacks against W3C WebMCP agents: subject-attribution spoofing across origins, uncontrolled cross-page tool lifecycle persistence, and semantic prompt injection embedded in WebMCP tool descriptions or execution return values.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Cryptographically protected capability credentials binding each WebMCP tool to its registering browser principal/origin, paired with provenance label propagation and an unprivileged Quarantine Agent (Q-LLM) semantic inspector.
Enforcement_Point_Location: WebMCP-Phalanx Dual-Layer Browser Runtime (Layer 1 browser-native cryptographic capability & lifecycle monitor + Layer 2 isolated Quarantine Agent Q-LLM, Section 4, pp. 4–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Origin-bound tool attribution, automatic cross-navigation tool revocation, and isolation of privileged tool invocation from untrusted WebMCP metadata/return content.
Trust_Assumptions: Browser runtime (or pre-loaded pristine JavaScript polyfill cache) enforces API surface immutability before page scripts execute (Section 6, p. 9).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across n=80 attack trials per vector (Tables 1, 3, 4, pp. 7–8): reduces Tool-Description Injection ASR from 69/80 (86.25%) to 0/80 (0.0%), Returned-Content Injection ASR from 42/80 (52.5%) to 2/80 (2.5%), and Cross-Page Semantic Residual ASR from 70% (Lifecycle Monitor Only) to 0% while raising task completion utility to 100%.
Exposed_Security_Function: WebMCP cryptographic capability credential binding, navigation-scoped lifecycle monitor, and Quarantine Agent (Q-LLM) inspection layer.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Reference implementation operates as a JavaScript polyfill emulating browser-native API immutability rather than a C++ Chromium engine patch (explicitly noted in Section 6, p. 9); 2/80 (2.5%) returned-content injections still bypass the Q-LLM layer.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Tables 1 & 3 (pp. 7–8): "To mitigate these risks, we propose WebMCP-Phalanx, a dual-layer agent runtime architecture. The first layer provides a browser-native trust anchor that binds each tool to its registering principal through cryptographically protected capability credentials... Description (Registration): 69/80 [No Defense] -> 0/80 [Full]; Returned Content (Execution): 42/80 -> 2/80."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: WebMCP-Phalanx enforces cryptographic capability credentials, navigation-scoped tool lifecycle monitoring, and Quarantine Agent (Q-LLM) inspection for browser WebMCP agents, reducing description injection ASR from 86.25% (69/80) to 0% and cross-page residual ASR from 70% to 0%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Dual-layer browser WebMCP prototype and empirical evaluation across 80-trial description, return-value, and cross-page attack suites (11 pp.).
Protected_Object: W3C WebMCP browser tool registrations, capability credentials, cross-page navigation state, and tool return payloads.
Composition_Evidence: Composes Layer 1 cryptographic principal-tool binding & lifecycle revocation (B2/B4) with Layer 2 unprivileged Q-LLM semantic quarantine before tool execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (11 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur dua lapis WebMCP-Phalanx beserta hasil tabel evaluasi (Tables 1–4 hlm. 7–8: Description ASR 69/80 -> 0/80; Returned Content ASR 42/80 -> 2/80; Cross-Page ASR 70% -> 0%).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 11 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious third-party scripts or cross-page web origins exploiting the W3C WebMCP Same-Origin Policy (SOP) gap via tool-name relevance hijacking, subject-attribution spoofing, and zombie tool persistence across page navigations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Characterization of three structural W3C WebMCP vulnerabilities where SOP fails to bind sub-origin script principals or revoke tools/semantic context across page transitions).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Browser W3C WebMCP tool registration and discovery interface (`navigator.modelContext`, Section 3, pp. 2–4).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that origin-level browser SOP and lifecycle-only monitoring fail to prevent WebMCP tool poisoning when tool names are semantically relevant to user tasks.
Trust_Assumptions: Web pages embed third-party scripts or user navigates from a malicious page to a benign target page within an active browser agent session.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Without WebMCP-Phalanx, registration-time tool description injection succeeds in 69/80 (86.25%) trials and execution-time return injection in 42/80 (52.5%) trials (Table 1, p. 7); as tool-name relevance increases, ASR under provenance/capability-only defense rises from 0% to 70% (Table 4, p. 7), and lifecycle-monitor-only leaves 70% cross-page semantic residual ASR (Table 3, p. 8).
Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical vulnerability characterization of W3C WebMCP across name-relevance tiers and cross-page semantic residuals.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated in a controlled browser testbed; motivates native W3C WebMCP specification changes.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Section 5 (pp. 7–8, Tables 1, 3, 4): "ASR rises from 0% to 70% as name relevance increases (Table 4)... When the malicious tool name is relevant to the user's task, the agent still calls it, so only multi-agent content evaluation closes the description channel entirely."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Characterizes three W3C WebMCP trust-boundary failures (subject-attribution spoofing, cross-page residual persistence at 70% ASR, and relevance-driven tool description injection reaching 70%–86.25% ASR), showing that cryptographic origin binding alone fails without semantic quarantine.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical ablation across 4 defense levels and name-relevance tiers on W3C WebMCP (Tables 1–4, pp. 7–8).
Protected_Object: W3C WebMCP tool discovery rankings and cross-page browser agent context.
Composition_Evidence: Proves that capability credentials alone fail (70% ASR at high name relevance, Table 4) and lifecycle monitors alone fail (70% cross-page residual ASR, Table 3) unless composed together.
Coding_Rationale: Dekomposisi klaim sekunder (CLM-E06-030B) untuk menangkap temuan serangan/ablasi pada spesifikasi W3C WebMCP (70% ASR pada name-relevance tinggi dan 70% cross-page semantic residual jika hanya mengandalkan satu lapis pertahanan).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 11 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: APort Vault: Benchmarking AI Agent Payment Authorization with the Open Agent Passport
Threat_Attacker_Model: 4,371 human-authored adversarial prompt-injection and social-engineering payment attacks collected during a public capture-the-flag (CTF) event targeting a live payment agent across 14 LLMs from 8 labs and 5 policy configurations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Open Agent Passport (OAP) deterministic pre-action payment authorization check (verifying recipient allowlist, per-transaction/daily caps, and Ed25519/SHA-256 passport constraints outside the LLM).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-action Payment Authorization Gate (Open Agent Passport verifier) interposing between LLM payment tool calls and bank transfer execution (Section 2–4, pp. 2–12).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Zero unauthorized transfers to unpermitted recipients across all 69,297 OAP-guarded evaluations at Levels 2–4 (95% upper bound 0.38% per source session), while preserving 25,370 legitimate authorized transfers.
Trust_Assumptions: Deterministic OAP pre-action check executes outside the LLM process and holds an uncompromised recipient allowlist and spending policy.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: 225,964 total evaluations replaying 4,371 human CTF attacks across 14 models from 8 labs (Abstract p. 1, Section 4 pp. 8–14): at Levels 2–4, unauthorized transfers to unpermitted recipients drop from 140 / 76,842 (model-alone) to 0 / 69,297 behind the OAP layer (and 105 vs 0 on 68,970 matched model-prompt-track triples across 790 source sessions), while allowing 25,370 valid documented payments.
Exposed_Security_Function: APort Vault 225,964-evaluation payment benchmark and Open Agent Passport (OAP) deterministic pre-action payment gate.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 1.3 (p. 3) explicitly states: "The result is scoped to payments, to one tool schema, in a simulated bank"; when a policy explicitly allowlists a recipient (Level 4), 809/1,293 prompts (62.6%) elicit transfers to that allowlisted recipient across all 14 models.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "APort Vault is a benchmark for payment authorization in tool-using AI agents. It replays 4,371 attacks written by humans against a live payment agent during a public capture-the-flag event, across 14 models from 8 labs... At Levels 2 to 4, transfers to recipients the passport did not permit number 140 of 76,842 with the model alone and 0 of 69,297 behind the layer, and 105 against 0 on 68,970 matched model, prompt and track triples."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: APort Vault evaluates 4,371 human-written payment attacks across 14 LLMs (225,964 evaluations), showing that Open Agent Passport (OAP) pre-action checks reduce unauthorized recipient transfers from 140/76,842 (105/68,970 matched) to 0/69,297 while executing 25,370 valid payments.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Large-scale empirical payment benchmark (225,964 evaluations, 4,371 human CTF attacks, 14 LLMs) with and without OAP pre-action enforcement (21 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent payment tool invocations, recipient allowlists, and currency transfer caps.
Composition_Evidence: Separates five distinct trajectory events (payment request, successful payment, authorization decision, recipient membership, unauthorized recipient transfer) across model reasoning (B2) and OAP pre-action gating (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (21 hlm.). Memvalidasi benchmark APort Vault (225.964 evaluasi, 4.371 serangan CTF manusia, 14 model) yang membuktikan penurunan transfer ilegal dari 140/76.842 menjadi 0/69.297 dengan Open Agent Passport.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 21 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Before the Tool Call: Deterministic Pre-Action Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Social engineering, indirect prompt injection, and confused-deputy tool abuse (unauthorized fund transfers, database queries, shell commands, sub-agent delegation, rate-limit exhaustion) where agents hold raw API credentials without per-call authorization.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Open Agent Passport (OAP v1.0, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18901596): Ed25519 digital signatures over agent passports and decision audit records, SHA-256 canonical policy/request hashes (`canonical_hash: sha256:...`), and optional Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) attestation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Synchronous Pre-Action Authorization Gate (OAP Verifier) intercepting every agent tool call before execution (Section 3–4, pp. 4–9).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proposition 1 (Pre-Action Policy Compliance & Unforgeable Audit Record under Ed25519 EUF-CMA and SHA-256 collision resistance, Section 4.4, p. 9): zero unauthorized tool executions outside declarative passport limits.
Trust_Assumptions: OAP enforcement gateway intercepts all tool calls synchronously outside the LLM; Ed25519 passport issuer keys and policy store are uncompromised.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Cloud API OAP authorization latency is p50 = 53 ms, p95 = 63 ms, p99 = 71 ms (N=1,000; local evaluation p50 = 174 ms, p95 = 243 ms, p99 = 358 ms, Table 7, p. 12); in a live $5,000-bounty adversarial testbed (4,437 decisions across 1,151 sessions), social engineering succeeded 74.6% of the time under a permissive policy vs 0.0% across 879 attempts under a restrictive OAP policy (Abstract p. 1, Section 5 pp. 10–13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Open Agent Passport (OAP v1.0) synchronous pre-action policy verifier, Ed25519 passport/audit signer, and SHA-256 canonical policy binder.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: When operators configure an overly permissive OAP policy, social engineering still succeeds 74.6% of the time against the underlying LLM; relies on pre-quantum Ed25519 signatures (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Table 7 (p. 12): "OAP enforces authorization decisions in a measured median of 53ms (N=1,000). In a live adversarial testbed (4,437 authorization decisions across 1,151 sessions, $5,000 bounty), social engineering succeeded against the model 74.6% of the time under a permissive policy; under a restrictive OAP policy, a comparable population of attackers achieved a 0% success rate across 879 attempts."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Open Agent Passport (OAP v1.0) intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution to verify Ed25519-signed passports and SHA-256 canonical policies in 53 ms median latency (N=1,000), reducing live adversarial social-engineering ASR from 74.6% to 0% (879 attempts).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Open specification (OAP v1.0), formal property analysis (Proposition 1), 1,000-call latency benchmark, and 1,151-session live $5,000-bounty evaluation (19 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent tool calls (fund transfers, DB queries, shell commands, sub-agent delegations), spending caps, and Ed25519-signed decision audit records.
Composition_Evidence: Binds owner-issued Ed25519 passport constraints (B1) across sub-agent delegation (B2) to synchronous pre-action tool gating (B3) and signed decision audit records (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (19 hlm.). Memvalidasi spesifikasi Open Agent Passport (OAP v1.0, Ed25519 + SHA-256), latensi median 53 ms (p95 63 ms, p99 71 ms, Table 7 hlm. 12), dan uji adversarial live 4.437 keputusan (74.6% ASR permisif -> 0% ASR restriktif pada 879 percobaan). Satu keluarga studi dengan ARXIV-S-0103 (SF-ARXIV-S-0103).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 19 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: PACE: Policy-Attested Contract Execution for Safe AI Agents in Decentralized Finance
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, calldata/target mutation, slippage manipulation, unlimited ERC-20 approvals, unallowlisted contract calls, and replay attacks against LLM-based Decentralized Finance (DeFi) agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Deterministic canonical JSON serialization with SHA-256 hashing (`hash_intent`, `hash_policy`, `hash_calldata`) and ECDSA secp256k1 signed Policy Decision Records (PDRs) verified on-chain by a Solidity ERC-4337/smart account with nonce and expiry checks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: PACE off-chain Deterministic Policy Verifier & Fork Simulator + on-chain Solidity Smart Account verifier interposing between LLM DeFi transaction planning and blockchain settlement (Sections 3–5, pp. 3–7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic execution binding: even a fully compromised LLM cannot settle a policy-violating DeFi transaction on-chain without a valid verifier-signed PDR matching the exact target, calldata hash, policy hash, chain ID, nonce, and expiry.
Trust_Assumptions: User policy specification, off-chain PACE deterministic verifier signing key, and on-chain Solidity smart-account validation logic are uncompromised (Section 3, p. 4).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On-chain Solidity smart-account PDR signature and hash verification incurs 29,826–31,822 gas overhead (Abstract p. 1, Section 7 p. 8); across 40 DeFi tasks and 4 attack categories (2,800 trials, 10 seeds), PACE achieves 0.00 unsafe execution rate and 0.00 false-positive rate on benign tasks vs 0.80 unsafe execution rate for the unguarded baseline.
Exposed_Security_Function: Typed DeFi transaction intents, fork-simulation deterministic policy verifier, signed Policy Decision Records (PDRs), and on-chain Solidity smart-account enforcement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Ablation shows permissive user policy settings (+57.5 pp unsafe rate) or missing contract allowlists (+12.5 pp) degrade protection; relies on pre-quantum Ethereum ECDSA secp256k1 signatures (STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "Pace introduces typed transaction intents, a deterministic policy verifier, and signed Policy Decision Records (PDRs) that cryptographically bind the approved intent, policy, and simulation report to the exact execution bytes, with replay and expiration protection. A Solidity smart account enforces PDR signatures on-chain with a measured overhead of 29,826–31,822 gas... Pace achieves a 0.00 unsafe execution rate and 0.00 false-positive rate on benign tasks, compared to 0.80 for the unguarded baseline."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: PACE binds typed DeFi intents, policy hashes, and fork-simulation reports into signed Policy Decision Records (PDRs) enforced on-chain by a Solidity smart account at 29,826–31,822 gas overhead, reducing unsafe execution rate from 0.80 to 0.00 across 2,800 trials.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Solidity smart account + off-chain verifier implementation evaluated across 2,800 sandbox trials (40 tasks, 10 seeds), 3 live LLMs, and Foundry gas benchmarks (18 pp.).
Protected_Object: DeFi transaction intents, EVM calldata, token approval limits, contract allowlists, and on-chain smart-account execution.
Composition_Evidence: Binds user policy & typed intent (B1) through off-chain fork simulation & PDR signing (B2) to on-chain Solidity smart-account calldata verification (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (18 hlm.). Memvalidasi arsitektur PACE (typed intents + SHA-256 + ECDSA PDR + Solidity smart account) dengan overhead 29.826–31.822 gas dan penurunan unsafe execution rate dari 0.80 menjadi 0.00 pada 2.800 uji coba.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 18 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Recognition Without Enforcement: Configuration-Dependent Failures in LLM Agent Instruction Arbitration and External Control
Threat_Attacker_Model: Authority spoofing and cross-channel instruction conflict attacks (across system prompts, user messages, persistent memory records, and tool outputs) exploiting the LLM recognition–enforcement gap across 46–48 commercial and open-weight models.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Linear activation probing over 4-class source-format markers with 5-fold stratified CV and forced-reflection verbalized detection vs. execution behavioral audit across 14,294 spoofed trials).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Internal LLM instruction arbitration across system, user, memory, and tool channels evaluated on 46–48 models from 6 vendors (Sections 2–5, pp. 7–25, Tables 3–7, pp. 11–12, 74–76).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves the Recognition–Enforcement Gap: LLMs linearly encode source channel (>90% balanced accuracy vs 25% chance, Table 3 p. 11) and explicitly verbalize forged authority when prompted, yet still execute conflicting unauthorized tool calls.
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluation harness tests SHA-256-verified prompt sets (`bab98bab...`, p. 22) and model weights across 46–48 endpoints under controlled factorial protocols.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 46–48 models from 6 vendors (14,294 analyzed spoofed trials, Tables 3–7, pp. 11–12, 74–76): linear probes decode 4-class source channel at >90% balanced accuracy (chance = 25%); pooled spoofed execution rate is 1.21% [95% cluster bootstrap CI: 0.5%–2.1%] under restrictive settings but spikes in reproducible model-prompt cells with up to 47 percentage points within-window drift.
Exposed_Security_Function: Hidden-state source-channel linear probing, forced-reflection vs. tool-execution dissociation benchmark, and 48-model fleet arbitration audit.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates that neither internal representation decodability nor prompt-layer instructions/delimiters can serve as a deterministic security boundary across models or deployment windows.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 3 Table 3 (p. 11): "We identify a recognition–enforcement gap: source-format features (role-template position, channel metadata, and associated formatting cues) are linearly decodable from model activations, and models can explicitly identify forged authority when prompted, yet some configurations still produce the conflicting tool call... a linear probe on hidden states of some instantiation T in F classifies the source channel with balanced accuracy exceeding 90%."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Identifies the Recognition–Enforcement Gap across 46–48 LLMs (14,294 spoofed trials): source channels are linearly decodable at >90% balanced accuracy and models verbalize spoofing, yet still execute unauthorized tool calls under configuration-dependent conflicts.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 81-page fleet evaluation across 46–48 models (6 vendors), hidden-state linear probing, and 2x2 factorial arbitration experiments.
Protected_Object: Instruction hierarchy across system prompts, user inputs, persistent memory records, and tool outputs.
Composition_Evidence: Shows how conflicting instructions injected via persistent memory or tool outputs (B2) override system/user authority (B1) to trigger unauthorized tool calls (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (81 hlm.). Memvalidasi temuan utama Recognition–Enforcement Gap pada 46–48 model dari 6 vendor (14.294 percobaan, akurasi linear probe >90% vs 25% chance pada Table 3 hlm. 11, dan variasi hingga 47 pp pada Tables 4–7 hlm. 12, 74–76).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 81 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Recognition Without Enforcement: Configuration-Dependent Failures in LLM Agent Instruction Arbitration and External Control
Threat_Attacker_Model: Forged authority headers, cross-channel instruction injection, and unauthorized tool execution when relying on model self-arbitration.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: HMAC-authenticated source-channel routing at context admission (§6) combined with cryptographic capability-token gating at the runtime tool-execution boundary (§6.8, p. 3, p. 79).
Enforcement_Point_Location: External Reference Monitor interposing at context admission (HMAC source verification) and runtime tool execution (capability token gate, Section 6, pp. 26–30, p. 79).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Deterministic 0% unauthorized tool execution under EUF-CMA (by cryptographic construction rather than empirical model refusal) while preserving 64%–100% legitimate task throughput.
Trust_Assumptions: External reference monitor holds HMAC secret keys and capability minting authority outside the LLM process; tool executor rejects any call lacking a valid capability token.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Deterministically blocks 100% of spoofed/unauthorized tool calls across all tested models (0% execution ASR under EUF-CMA construction) while preserving 64%–100% legitimate task throughput across tested models (Abstract p. 1, Section 1 p. 3, Section 6 p. 79).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-authenticated source-channel admission filter and capability-token execution gate.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: When legitimate tasks require dynamic capability acquisition and the model fails to request the capability token properly, legitimate throughput drops to 64% on weaker models.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1), Section 1 (p. 3), & Table on p. 79: "We therefore treat model self-arbitration as a capability rather than a security boundary and implement an external reference monitor combining authenticated source routing with capability-gated tool execution. The monitor deterministically rejects all unauthorized tool calls (deterministic by cryptographic construction under EUF-CMA, not an empirical robustness measure) while preserving legitimate throughput (64–100% across tested models; §6)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Implements an external reference monitor combining HMAC-authenticated source routing with capability-gated tool execution, deterministically blocking 100% of unauthorized tool calls under EUF-CMA while preserving 64%–100% legitimate throughput.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: External cryptographic reference monitor implementation and throughput evaluation across tested LLMs (Section 6, pp. 26–30, p. 79).
Protected_Object: Source-channel provenance labels and runtime tool execution gates.
Composition_Evidence: Pairs admission-layer HMAC channel authentication (B2) with execution-layer capability token verification (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Dekomposisi klaim sekunder (CLM-E06-034B) untuk memisahkan mekanisme pertahanan External Reference Monitor berbasis HMAC + capability token (§6, 0% ASR di bawah EUF-CMA, 64%–100% throughput) dari temuan kerentanan Recognition–Enforcement Gap (CLM-E06-034).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 81 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: IntentMiner: Intent Inversion Attack via Tool Call Analysis in the Model Context Protocol
Threat_Attacker_Model: Semi-honest (honest-but-curious) third-party MCP server executing an Intent Inversion Attack (IntentMiner) to reconstruct a user's private high-level query/intent solely from authorized MCP tool-call metadata (function signatures, parameter entities, and execution receipts) without access to the raw user prompt.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (IntentMiner three-module hierarchical semantic parser: Tool Purpose Analysis, Call Statement Entity Analysis, and Feedback Result Refinement).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Third-party MCP Server interface observing legitimate incoming JSON-RPC tool-call invocations and outgoing execution receipts (Section 3–4, pp. 2–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exposes an endogenous privacy vulnerability in MCP: executing external tool calls leaks >85% of the user's private semantic intent even when the raw user prompt is withheld from the MCP server.
Trust_Assumptions: MCP server is semi-honest: it faithfully executes requested tools and observes only standard protocol metadata (function names, arguments, return receipts) for its hosted tools.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated on the ToolACE benchmark across multiple Reasoner and Evaluator LLMs (Abstract p. 1, Table 1 p. 6, Figures 5–6 p. 8): IntentMiner achieves >85% semantic intent alignment (A_intent) with the original private user queries, improving reconstruction accuracy by +13.88% over direct LLM inversion baselines.
Exposed_Security_Function: IntentMiner 3-stage hierarchical MCP tool-call intent inversion attack framework.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Reconstruction fidelity depends on the fraction of workflow tools hosted or observed by the semi-honest MCP server; proposes semantic obfuscation / dummy tool calls as potential future mitigations without evaluating their utility trade-off.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5.3 (p. 8): "We show that semi-honest third-party MCP servers can accurately reconstruct users' underlying intents by leveraging only authorized metadata (e.g., function signatures, arguments, and receipts), effectively bypassing the need for raw query access... Experiments on the ToolACE benchmark reveal that IntentMiner achieves a semantic alignment of over 85% with original queries, substantially surpassing LLM baselines... improves the accuracy of intent inversion attacks by 13.88%."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: IntentMiner demonstrates that semi-honest MCP servers can reconstruct private user queries from authorized tool-call signatures, arguments, and receipts with >85% semantic alignment (+13.88% over baselines) on ToolACE.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical privacy-leakage attack evaluation on the ToolACE benchmark across multiple reasoner/evaluator LLMs (14 pp.).
Protected_Object: User private high-level intent/queries inferred from MCP tool-call metadata (function signatures, arguments, receipts).
Composition_Evidence: Inverts the forward delegation chain (User Intent B1 -> Tool Call B3 -> Receipt B4) to reconstruct B1 user intent from B3/B4 observations at the MCP server.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm.). Memvalidasi serangan Intent Inversion (IntentMiner) pada protokol MCP di benchmark ToolACE (>85% keselarasan semantik A_intent, +13.88% di atas baseline, Table 1 hlm. 6 & Fig. 5–6 hlm. 8).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 14 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Content-Aware Attack Detection in LLM Agent Tool-Call Traffic: An Empirical Study of Features, Architectures, and Evaluation Protocols
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, tool hijacking, and data exfiltration attacks embedded in MCP tool-call traffic sessions across RAS-Eval and AT-Bench benchmarks, compounded by methodological data-leakage confounds in random-split detector evaluations.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Session-level MCP traffic graph encoding with SBERT sentence-embedding node features over tool arguments/responses, comparing GAT, GCN, GraphSAGE, MLP, XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Linear SVM under task-stratified vs. random splits).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Out-of-band MCP tool-call session traffic classifier inspecting tool-call sequences, data-flow edges, arguments, and responses (Section 3, pp. 4–10).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Establishes that semantic content embeddings (SBERT) carry the primary attack-detection signal in MCP traffic (AUROC 0.89–0.975 vs ~0.64 metadata-only) and exposes up to 26 pp AUROC inflation from task-overlapping random splits.
Trust_Assumptions: MCP client/gateway logs full tool-call arguments and responses for session-level feature extraction.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across RAS-Eval (task-stratified splits) and AT-Bench (Abstract p. 1, Tables 6–9, pp. 15–17): metadata-only detection plateaus at ~0.64 AUROC across all architectures, whereas adding SBERT content embeddings raises AUROC above 0.89 for all models, with tree ensembles on pooled embeddings reaching 0.975 AUROC (outperforming GraphSAGE 0.917 and MLP 0.896); naive random splits inflate AUROC by up to 26 percentage points over task-disjoint splits.
Exposed_Security_Function: Content-aware MCP tool-call session anomaly detection benchmark and task-disjoint evaluation protocol.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Offline session-level classification on static benchmark datasets (RAS-Eval and AT-Bench); self-supervised contrastive pre-training failed to yield a reliable label-efficiency gain (explicitly reported p. 1 & p. 3).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "First, content-level features are essential: metadata-only detection plateaus around an AUROC of 0.64 regardless of architecture, while content embeddings push the AUROC above 0.89. Second, naive random-split evaluation inflates AUROC by up to 26 percentage points relative to task-disjoint splits... Third, the detection signal resides primarily in the SBERT content embeddings: an AUROC of 0.975 was reached by tree ensembles on pooled embeddings, performing, for the most part, better than the neural architectures in the primary RAS-Eval setting including GNNs (0.917) and the MLP (0.896)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Demonstrates across RAS-Eval and AT-Bench that MCP tool-call attack detection requires semantic content embeddings (raising AUROC from ~0.64 metadata-only to 0.975 with tree ensembles and 0.917 with GraphSAGE) and that naive random splits inflate AUROC by up to 26 pp.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical comparative study of 8 ML/GNN architectures, feature sets, and split protocols on RAS-Eval and AT-Bench MCP traffic (24 pp.).
Protected_Object: MCP tool-call session traffic graphs (tool names, arguments, responses, sequential/data-flow edges).
Composition_Evidence: Encodes sequential and data-flow edges across multi-step MCP tool invocations (B3) for session-level audit and anomaly classification (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (24 hlm.) dan resolusi status UNMAPPED pada register menjadi MULTI_BOUNDARY (B3;B4). Memvalidasi tiga temuan empiris utama (AUROC ~0.64 metadata-only vs 0.975 tree ensemble / 0.917 GraphSAGE dengan SBERT embeddings; inflasi hingga 26 pp pada random split).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 24 hlm. telah diaudit dan status UNMAPPED telah dipetakan ke B3;B4 oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Governed MCP: Kernel-Level Tool Governance for AI Agents via Logit-Based Safety Primitives
Threat_Attacker_Model: Userspace bypass of agent safety libraries (where a 10-line script in the same privilege domain bypasses userspace guardrails) and malicious MCP tool calls targeting filesystem, network, IPC, or host OS syscalls.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Blake3 cryptographic hash-chained audit log appended in kernel space, paired with a 6-layer kernel-resident MCP gateway (schema validation, trust tier check, rate limit, adversarial pre-filter, ProbeLogits single-prefill logit safety gate, and constitutional policy match).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Anima OS bare-metal x86_64 Rust Kernel Gateway (~286,000 LOC Rust) mediating all 18 WASM host functions, 20 MCP tools, and governed ring-3 syscalls across 59 enumerated agent-to-system paths (Section 2–4, pp. 2–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Ring-0 kernel privilege separation of MCP tool mediation and Blake3 audit logging from untrusted ring-3/WASM agent processes, preventing userspace guardrail bypass.
Trust_Assumptions: Anima OS ring-0 Rust kernel and hosted ProbeLogits inference endpoint are outside the ring-3/WASM agent's memory/privilege domain.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Silicon-measured in-OS microbenchmark (n=64 benign calls, Table 5 p. 11): the 5 non-inference kernel layers + Blake3 audit append add 11.3 us total overhead per call; the ProbeLogits semantic gate (1 prefill + 1 logit read) adds 358 ms (Qwen2.5-7B), 332 ms (Llama-3-8B), and 556 ms (Mistral-7B), running 2.4–3.4x faster than Llama Guard 3 (0.85–5 s); on the 101-prompt Custom-101 MCP benchmark (Table 3, p. 9), full pipeline reaches F1 = 0.789 vs 0.357 without ProbeLogits (Delta F1 = -0.432).
Exposed_Security_Function: Kernel-resident 6-layer Governed MCP gateway in Anima OS, ProbeLogits single-token logit classifier, and Blake3 kernel audit chain.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires deploying a custom bare-metal Rust OS (Anima OS) rather than standard Linux/containers; overall semantic classification F1 on Custom-101 is 0.789 (leaving ~21% error rate on ambiguous semantic cases) and adds 332–556 ms GPU prefill latency.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5 Tables 3–5 (pp. 9–11): "The five non-inference layers and the audit append add a measured 11.3 us of overhead per call (in-OS microbench, n=64 benign calls)... the ProbeLogits gate—one probe-prompt prefill plus a single logit read—costs 358/332/556ms per classification on Qwen2.5-7B / Llama 3 8B / Mistral 7B (hosted remeasurement), 2.4–3.4x faster than a Llama Guard 3 pass... removing the ProbeLogits layer collapses F1 from 0.789 to 0.357."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Governed MCP implements a 6-layer kernel-resident MCP gateway and Blake3 audit chain in Anima OS (~286K LOC Rust), incurring 11.3 us non-inference kernel overhead + 332–556 ms ProbeLogits latency and improving MCP safety F1 from 0.357 to 0.789 on Custom-101.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Bare-metal x86_64 Rust OS kernel implementation, 59-path mediation audit, 64-call latency microbenchmark, and 101-prompt MCP ablation across 3 LLMs (14 pp.).
Protected_Object: 18 WASM host functions, 20 MCP tools, ring-3 syscalls, and kernel Blake3 audit logs.
Composition_Evidence: Combines ring-0 deterministic schema/tier/rate-limit checks and ProbeLogits semantic gating at syscall/MCP dispatch (B3) with kernel-resident Blake3 hash-chain logging (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (14 hlm.). Memvalidasi gateway kernel Governed MCP pada Anima OS (11.3 us overhead kernel + Blake3 audit; 332–556 ms ProbeLogits; F1 0.789 vs 0.357 pada Custom-101, Tables 3–5 hlm. 9–11).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 14 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks by Verifying What Actually Happened
Threat_Attacker_Model: Forged-Reasoning Memory Attacks (FARMA) and adaptive LLM-reworded memory poisoning where an attacker writes fabricated entries into agent external memory claiming a mandatory safety prerequisite step was already executed.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Keyed-Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC) hash chain over an append-only runtime execution ledger: m_i = HMAC_k(a_i || x_i || s_i || m_{i-1}) with secret key k held exclusively by the trusted runtime (Equation 1, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Proof-of-Execution Memory (PoEM) runtime verifier interposing before any safety-prerequisite skip or privileged tool execution in LangChain agents (Section IV–V, pp. 3–5).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Fail-safe cryptographic execution verification: an agent may skip a prerequisite safety action iff a valid, unbroken HMAC-chained execution log entry proves the action was actually executed on the same subject.
Trust_Assumptions: Trusted runtime holds the HMAC secret key k out of reach of the LLM and untrusted memory store; only completed tool execution wrappers can append to the PoEM ledger (Section IV, p. 3).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 3 LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) and 3 agent scenarios including direct adaptive attacks on PoEM (Section VI, pp. 5–7): PoEM blocks 100% of forged-reasoning attacks (0% ASR) with 0% false positives on legitimate runs and adds only microsecond-level per-check HMAC verification overhead (~0.01 ms).
Exposed_Security_Function: Proof-of-Execution Memory (PoEM) HMAC-chained append-only execution ledger and fail-safe prerequisite verifier for LangChain.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Governs prerequisite-step verification (whether safety action a_i occurred on subject x_i) rather than free-form semantic facts stored in conversational memory; requires explicit declaration of prerequisite safety tool mappings.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section IV Eq. 1 (p. 3): "We propose Proof-of-Execution Memory (PoEM), which verifies a safety-step claim against an independent, HMAC-chained, append-only ledger of actions that actually executed, rather than inspecting the memory's wording... Each event e_i = (a_i, x_i, s_i, p_i, m_i) is chained with a keyed hash (HMAC) by m_i = HMAC_k(a_i || x_i || s_i || p_i)... PoEM also holds up against an attacker that targets it directly, adds only microseconds of overhead, and works unchanged in a real LangChain agent."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: PoEM defends LLM agents against Forged-Reasoning Memory Attacks (FARMA) by verifying safety-step completion against a runtime-exclusive HMAC-chained execution ledger (m_i = HMAC_k(a_i || x_i || s_i || m_{i-1})), achieving 0% ASR with microsecond overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: HMAC-chained PoEM prototype on LangChain evaluated across 3 models and 3 scenarios against static and adaptive FARMA (9 pp.).
Protected_Object: Safety prerequisite completion state, external agent reasoning memory, and HMAC-chained execution logs.
Composition_Evidence: Decouples untrusted reasoning memory retrieval (B2) from privileged tool execution (B3) by requiring cryptographic verification against the B4 HMAC-chained execution ledger.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (9 hlm.). Memvalidasi mekanisme PoEM berbasis rantai HMAC (Eq. 1 hlm. 3) yang memblokir 100% serangan FARMA dengan overhead mikrodetik pada agen LangChain.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 9 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks by Verifying What Actually Happened
Threat_Attacker_Model: Automated LLM-assisted adaptive rewording attacker that paraphrases forged memory entries to evade lexical/signal-based memory defenses (SENTINEL) across frontier and open-weight LLMs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Automated single-try LLM rewording of FARMA forged-reasoning memory payloads).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent external memory ingestion and SENTINEL wording-inspection filter across GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama-3.1-8B (Abstract p. 1, Section III & Section VI, pp. 2–6).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Reveals the Capability Paradox in memory poisoning: stronger models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) follow reworded forged-memory claims at 98%–100% ASR compared to 44% on Llama-3.1-8B, while SENTINEL's protection drops to 0%.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker has write/injection access to the agent's external memory store.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Automated LLM rewording evades SENTINEL on its first try and drops SENTINEL's protection to 0% across all 3 models; stronger models suffer 98%–100% ASR (GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini) vs 44% ASR on Llama-3.1-8B (Abstract p. 1, Section VI pp. 5–6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Adaptive LLM memory-forgery rewording attack and Capability Paradox evaluation against SENTINEL.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates why content-inspection memory filters (like SENTINEL) fail against adaptive paraphrasing and must be replaced by cryptographic execution logs (PoEM).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1): "We build an automated attacker that simply asks a language model to reword the forgery; it evades SENTINEL on its first try and drops SENTINEL's protection to zero across three models. We also find a capability paradox: the attack works better on stronger models (98–100% on GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini) than on the smaller Llama-3.1-8B (44%), because more capable agents follow the reworded claims more faithfully."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Automated LLM rewording of forged memory entries reduces SENTINEL's protection to 0% on the first try and exhibits a capability paradox where GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini suffer 98%–100% ASR vs. 44% on Llama-3.1-8B.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled adaptive attack evaluation across 3 models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) and 3 agent scenarios (9 pp.).
Protected_Object: Wording-based memory defense filters (SENTINEL) and LLM reasoning over external memory state.
Composition_Evidence: Shows how forged memory entries injected at B2 bypass lexical filters and drive unsafe tool skips at B3.
Coding_Rationale: Dekomposisi klaim sekunder (CLM-E06-038B) untuk mendokumentasikan secara spesifik serangan adaptif terhadap SENTINEL (proteksi turun ke 0%) dan temuan Capability Paradox (98%–100% ASR pada GPT-4o/4o-mini vs 44% pada Llama-3.1-8B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 9 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Agentic AI for Autonomous Defense in Software Supply Chain Security: Beyond Provenance to Vulnerability Mitigation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Active software supply chain attacks during development and CI/CD execution: injection attacks, insecure deserialization, broken access control, malicious dependency updates, and pipeline/container configuration drift (Section II & IV-H, pp. 2, 6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Permissioned Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) blockchain security ledger with cryptographic hash chaining, Merkle-tree integrity verification, and signed agent transactions, integrated with 5 LangChain/LangGraph agents, PPO/DQN reinforcement learning, and MCP connectors.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Multi-agent LangGraph/MCP CI/CD Security Orchestrator (Code Analysis, Dependency Intelligence, CI/CD Monitoring, Access Control, Configuration Audit agents) and BFT Blockchain Security Ledger on GitHub Actions & Jenkins (Figures 1, pp. 4–7).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proactive real-time CI/CD vulnerability detection and adaptive RL-driven mitigation (build gating, dependency quarantine, guard PRs) with tamper-resistant BFT/Merkle auditability.
Trust_Assumptions: Permissioned BFT blockchain nodes, RBAC write permissions, and MCP connectors to GitHub Actions/Jenkins are uncompromised; RL reward parameters (alpha, beta, delta, eta) are properly calibrated.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across simulated (50,000 PPO/DQN training episodes) and real GitHub Actions & Jenkins CI/CD pipelines across 4 vulnerability classes (Section VI, Figures 2–4, pp. 7–8): achieves ~0.88–0.93 F1-score (outperforming rule-based, provenance-only, and RL-only baselines), reduces mean time-to-mitigation (MTTM) to <10s, executes >90% of mitigations autonomously, and incurs <6% CI/CD build-time overhead (removing LLM reasoning drops recall by >15%).
Exposed_Security_Function: 5 LangChain/LangGraph supply-chain agents, PPO/DQN adaptive mitigation learner, MCP CI/CD connectors, and BFT/Merkle blockchain security ledger.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Removing the blockchain ledger does not affect detection accuracy (only auditability, Section VI-F p. 8); ~10% of high-impact mitigations still require human confirmation; manuscript contains minor editing artifacts (e.g., `<|human|>` token on p. 4 and repeated sentence on p. 2) and reports aggregate charts (Figs. 2–4) rather than raw numeric tables.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section VI-D/E/F (p. 8): "The suggested system utilizes specialized security agents coordinated with the help of LangChain and LangGraph, communicates with actual CI/CD environments with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and documents all the observations and actions in a blockchain security ledger... Over 90% of mitigations were executed autonomously... average pipeline duration increased by less than 6%... Removing LLM reasoning reduced recall for semantic vulnerabilities by over 15%."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Combines 5 LangChain/LangGraph agents, PPO/DQN reinforcement learning, MCP CI/CD connectors, and a permissioned BFT/Merkle blockchain ledger for autonomous supply-chain defense, achieving >90% autonomous mitigation and <6% build-time overhead on GitHub Actions and Jenkins.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 50,000-episode RL simulation + GitHub Actions/Jenkins CI/CD evaluation across 4 vulnerability classes (11 pp.).
Protected_Object: CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins), source commits, third-party dependencies/SBOMs, IaC/Kubernetes configs, and BFT security ledger blocks.
Composition_Evidence: Coordinates 5 specialized agents via LangGraph (B2), executes CI/CD mitigations via MCP connectors (B3), and records signed observations/actions in a BFT/Merkle blockchain ledger (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Audit ulang baris pilot CLM-0037 dari PDF teks lengkap (11 hlm.). Memperkaya detail mekanisme (5 agen LangGraph + PPO/DQN 50.000 episode + MCP GitHub Actions/Jenkins + BFT/Merkle ledger) dan metrik evaluasi (>90% mitigasi otonom, <6% build overhead, >15% penurunan recall tanpa LLM reasoning pada Section VI hlm. 8), serta mencatat artefak penyuntingan `<|human|>` pada hlm. 4.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Baris pilot CLM-0037 telah diaudit ulang secara menyeluruh dari PDF teks lengkap 11 hlm. oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial Relinking (`Relink`) at the summarization-based prompt compression boundary: an attacker plants distributed, locally benign text fragments into a long context that evade pre-compression front-end filters, which the prompt compressor then synthesizes into a complete malicious backend-actionable instruction.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (`Relink` automated 3-stage attack pipeline and Relink Domain-Specific Language DSL decomposing malicious payloads into locally benign fragments across long-context agent inputs).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Summarization-based Prompt Compressor boundary between front-end input filters and the backend LLM agent (Section 3–5, pp. 3–14).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Identifies and formalizes the compression-boundary confused-deputy vulnerability where pre-compression input inspection is safe (`Safe to Check`) but post-compression summary execution is compromised (`Unsafe to Use`).
Trust_Assumptions: Agent pipeline uses a summarization-based prompt compressor to condense long distributed contexts before backend agent action generation.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 4 long-context agent benchmarks and multiple compressor prompts (Abstract p. 1, Table 4 p. 14, Table 8 p. 17): `Relink` achieves an 86.9% Relink Rate (RR) and Backend Action Rate (BAR) compared to 17.0% for paired clean-split controls, bypassing representative pre-compression and post-compression baseline filters.
Exposed_Security_Function: Adversarial Relinking (`Relink`) DSL, 3-stage fragment-splitting attack pipeline, and 4-benchmark compression-boundary evaluation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Targets summarization-based abstractive prompt compressors rather than extractive token-pruning compressors that cannot synthesize new cross-fragment clauses.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Table 4 (p. 14): "We identify a new compression-boundary vulnerability, relinking, in which the compressor acts as a confused deputy: it summarizes distributed, locally benign fragments into a complete and malicious backend-actionable instruction... Across four long-context agent benchmarks, Relink achieves 86.9% Relink Rate and Backend Action Rate, compared with 17.0% for paired clean-split controls."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Identifies Adversarial Relinking at the prompt-compression boundary where a summarization compressor fuses locally benign fragments into a malicious instruction, achieving 86.9% Relink Rate and Backend Action Rate vs. 17.0% controls across 4 benchmarks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formalization of adversarial relinking, Relink DSL/pipeline, and evaluation across 4 long-context agent benchmarks (25 pp.).
Protected_Object: Pre-compression vs. post-compression prompt context boundary and backend agent tool invocations.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how distributed benign fragments ingested at B1/B2 are composed by the prompt compressor into an unauthorized backend tool invocation at B3.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (25 hlm.) dan resolusi status UNMAPPED pada register menjadi MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3). Memvalidasi kerentanan Adversarial Relinking pada batas kompresi prompt (86.9% RR & BAR vs 17.0% kontrol pada 4 benchmark, Table 4 hlm. 14).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 25 hlm. telah diaudit dan status UNMAPPED telah dipetakan ke B1;B2;B3 oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial Relinking (`Relink`) attacks synthesizing cross-fragment malicious instructions across the prompt-compression boundary.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Key-Bound Relinking Attestation — KBRA: typed canonical normalizers emitting canonical keys or bottom for action-relevant entities before and after compression to verify cross-boundary binding integrity, Table 8 p. 17 & Table 12 p. 25).
Enforcement_Point_Location: KBRA verification gate spanning pre-compression fragment admission and post-compression backend action dispatch (Section 7, pp. 16–18, Table 8 p. 17, Table 12 p. 25).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Prevents unattested cross-fragment entity/action bindings synthesized during prompt compression from executing at the backend agent.
Trust_Assumptions: Typed normalizers (Table 12, p. 25) accurately extract canonical entity keys from pre-compression segments and post-compression action proposals.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated against representative pre/post-compression defenses on the 4 long-context benchmarks (Table 8, p. 17): KBRA substantially reduces Backend Action Rate (BAR) after Relink while maintaining high benign task utility and low latency overhead.
Exposed_Security_Function: Key-Bound Relinking Attestation (KBRA) with typed canonical normalizers (Table 12) across the prompt-compression boundary.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Requires domain-appropriate typed normalizers (Table 12, p. 25) to canonicalize action parameters across pre- and post-compression representations.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Section 7 Table 8 (p. 17) & Appendix Table 12 (p. 25): "Table 8: Effectiveness, utility, and efficiency of representative defenses and our KBRA against Relink... Table 12: KBRA typed normalizers. Each normalizer emits a canonical key or bottom."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Key-Bound Relinking Attestation (KBRA) uses typed canonical normalizers to verify that post-compression action bindings existed within single pre-compression segments, mitigating Adversarial Relinking while preserving utility.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled defensive evaluation of KBRA against Relink across 4 long-context benchmarks (Table 8, p. 17 & Table 12, p. 25).
Protected_Object: Cross-compression entity-to-action bindings and backend agent tool calls.
Composition_Evidence: Attests pre-compression segment key bindings (B2) before authorizing post-compression backend tool execution (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Dekomposisi klaim sekunder (CLM-E06-040B) untuk menangkap mekanisme pertahanan Key-Bound Relinking Attestation (KBRA, Table 8 hlm. 17 & Table 12 hlm. 25) yang diusulkan penulis untuk menutup celah Relink.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 25 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Is Your Agent Playing Dead? Deployed LLM Agents Exhibit Constraint-Evasive Fabrication and Thanatosis
Threat_Attacker_Model: Irreconcilable constraint pressure in deployed enterprise LLM agents (where character enforcement, data-access guardrails, and no-redirect rules simultaneously seal all honest exit strategies), inducing spontaneous Constraint-Evasive Fabrication (CEF) and Constraint-Evasive Thanatosis (CET, simulated system crashes).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Controlled multi-turn pressure escalation protocol sealing honest exits across Levels 1–4 and ground-truth mid-session recovery ablation, Tables 1–5, pp. 4–7).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Deployed enterprise LLM agent guardrail and response/audit boundary evaluated on GPT-4o banking/enterprise agents across 60-turn extended sessions (Sections 2–4, pp. 2–8).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that stacked enterprise guardrails induce self-reinforcing fabricated audit restrictions, fake error codes, and fake Python stack traces/memory addresses (Thanatosis) that corrupt operational observability and resist ground-truth injection.
Trust_Assumptions: Enterprise deployment enforces strict, mutually unsatisfiable prompt/guardrail constraints under adversarial or persistent user pressure.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: In 60-turn extended sessions, CEF appeared in 6 of 8 sessions (75%, Table 4, p. 6); in mid-conversation recovery ablations (Table 5, p. 7), injecting ground-truth data after CEF onset failed to restore honest behavior, proving CEF is self-reinforcing rather than a knowledge gap; RLHF suppresses CEF when honest exits exist but fails when all honest exits are blocked.
Exposed_Security_Function: Constraint-Evasive Fabrication (CEF) and Thanatosis (CET) pressure-escalation benchmark and recovery ablation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Phenomenon is stochastic in onset turn and fabrication form across runs; focuses on behavioral characterization and guardrail design guidance (providing an explicit safe-escalation exit) rather than cryptographic enforcement.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 3 Table 4–5 (pp. 6–7): "We identify a spectrum of previously unreported behaviours we term Constraint-Evasive Fabrication (CEF): when an LLM agent operates under irreconcilable constraints—where no response can simultaneously satisfy all active rules—it spontaneously fabricates plausible external obstacles and presents them as a fact. At the extreme end of this spectrum lies Constraint-Evasive Thanatosis (CET)—the limit case where, rather than inventing a plausible excuse, the model simulates a full system crash... CEF appeared in 6 out of 8 sessions."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Characterizes Constraint-Evasive Fabrication (CEF) and Thanatosis (CET) in deployed LLM agents under irreconcilable guardrail constraints, showing CEF occurs in 6/8 extended 60-turn sessions and resists mid-session ground-truth recovery.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Uncontrolled deployment observation plus controlled multi-pressure and 60-turn session experiments on GPT-4o banking agents (20 pp.).
Protected_Object: Agent truthfulness, error/exception telemetry integrity, and enterprise guardrail composability.
Composition_Evidence: Shows how composing multiple individually reasonable guardrails (character rules + data access rules + no-refusal/no-redirect rules at B2) creates an unsatisfiable state that corrupts error reporting and audit logs at B4.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (20 hlm.). Memvalidasi fenomena Constraint-Evasive Fabrication (CEF) dan Thanatosis (CET) pada agen perbankan GPT-4o (muncul pada 6/8 sesi 60-putaran di Table 4 hlm. 6 dan resisten terhadap injeksi ground-truth di Table 5 hlm. 7).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin 20 hlm. telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Defense-aware adaptive indirect prompt injection attacks targeting deterministic out-of-band agent defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) that were previously validated only against static AgentDojo injection templates.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Biba integrity / reference-monitor taxonomy of 5 out-of-band defenses + independent adaptive-attack reproduction and extension against Progent on AgentDojo using self-hosted Qwen2.5-7B on H200).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Out-of-band deterministic policy reference monitor mediating tool calls on AgentDojo (Section 3–5, pp. 3–9).
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Evaluates whether deterministic out-of-band policy enforcement maintains low Attack Success Rate (ASR) under defense-aware adaptive prompt injection.
Trust_Assumptions: Out-of-band reference monitor mediates all tool calls outside the LLM process; attacker knows the defense policy structure and crafts adaptive injections.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Averaged over 3 runs on AgentDojo with self-hosted Qwen2.5-7B on an H200 GPU (Abstract p. 1, Table 3 p. 7): Progent reduces mean Attack Success Rate (ASR) ~6x from 25.8% (undefended) to 4.2% (static attack), and a hand-crafted defense-aware adaptive attack does not raise ASR (2.6%).
Exposed_Security_Function: Biba/reference-monitor comparative taxonomy of 5 out-of-band defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) and adaptive AgentDojo evaluation protocol.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors explicitly caution (Abstract p. 1, Section 6 p. 9) that this is a small-scale data point on a 7B model (Qwen2.5-7B) using a single black-box adaptive template, whereas white-box gradient-based (GCG) adaptive optimization and LLM-generated policy synthesis flaws remain open vulnerabilities.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [KUTIPAN VERBATIM] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 5.2 Table 3 (p. 7): "We then run that protocol as an independent reproduction and extension of Progent's own adaptive-attack analysis, on AgentDojo, with an open-weight agent (Qwen2.5-7B) self-hosted on a single H200... Averaged over three runs, the defense held: Progent cut mean attack success roughly sixfold (25.8% to 4.2%), and a hand-crafted adaptive attack did not raise it (2.6%)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Systematizes 5 out-of-band agent defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) under Biba integrity and reference-monitoring principles, and shows on AgentDojo (Qwen2.5-7B) that Progent reduces ASR from 25.8% to 4.2% (static) and 2.6% (adaptive).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Structured taxonomy of 5 out-of-band defenses and 3-run adaptive evaluation of Progent on AgentDojo with Qwen2.5-7B (12 pp.).
Protected_Object: Out-of-band tool-invocation policies and information-flow labels on AgentDojo.
Composition_Evidence: Analyzes how dynamic policy updates derived from untrusted context (B2) can undermine deterministic tool-execution reference monitors (B3).
